chapters.htmlContent:
QSell Enterprise: Master Implementor & Sales Enablement Guide

Welcome to the comprehensive operational manual for QSell, an enterprise-grade omnichannel commerce, inventory, route logistics, procurement, core double-entry accounting, and regulatory compliance platform.

This documentation suite is engineered specifically for System Implementors deploying and configuring customer organizations, and Sales Team Members & Solutions Consultants communicating the platform's value proposition, commercial return on investment (ROI), and competitive advantages to prospective businesses.

---

1. System Architecture from a Business Perspective

QSell replaces fragmented point solutions (separate e-commerce plugins, manual POS registers, disconnected spreadsheets, third-party courier dispatch apps, and standalone accounting software) with one unified, real-time operating system.

graph TD
    subgraph FrontOffice["Front-Office & Customer Channels"]
        WEB["Branded Web Storefront\n(Desktop & Mobile)"]
        POS["In-Store Point of Sale\n& Counter Orders"]
        QUOTE["Proforma Sales Quotes\n& Direct B2B Portal"]
    end

    subgraph Operations["Operations & Logistics Engine"]
        ORD["Order Stage Engine\n(Timestamped Milestones & SLAs)"]
        INV["Multi-Location WMS\n(Warehouses, Stores & Van Stock)"]
        DISP["Dispatch Board &\nRoute Run Sequencing"]
        RIDER["Rider Field Mobile App\n(Dropoffs, PIN & COD Collections)"]
    end

    subgraph Governance["Governance & Supply Chain"]
        APP["Runtime Approval Engine\n(Tiered Limits & Substitute Chains)"]
        PROC["Vendor Procurement\n(RFQs, POs, RGNs & 3-Way Match)"]
        VEND["Vendor Self-Service Portal\n(Bids, Acknowledgements & Invoices)"]
    end

    subgraph BackOffice["Back-Office Finance & Compliance"]
        AR["Accounts Receivable\n(Receipts, Wallets & Ageing)"]
        GL["General Ledger\n(Immutable Double-Entry Postings)"]
        BANK["Bank, Cash & Till\nReconciliation"]
        KRA["KRA eTIMS / TIMS\nReal-time Fiscal Signing"]
    end

    FrontOffice --> ORD
    ORD --> APP
    APP --> INV
    INV --> DISP
    DISP --> RIDER
    RIDER --> AR
    PROC --> VEND
    VEND --> INV
    AR --> GL
    BANK --> GL
    ORD --> KRA

The Six Operational Pillars

  1. Omnichannel Demand Capture: Unifies online storefront transactions, walk-in counter sales, telephone orders, and negotiated B2B proforma quotes into a single consolidated order stream.
  2. Immutable Inventory & Location Ledger: Tracks stock movements across central warehouses, regional retail stores, and mobile delivery vans in real time using true double-entry stock transactions with zero silent overrides.
  3. End-to-End Route Logistics & Door Collections: Manages localized delivery zones, dynamic delivery fee calculation (by distance, weight, or flat fee), rider dispatch runs, and reconciled Cash-on-Delivery (COD) or M-Pesa collections at the doorstep.
  4. Controlled Procurement & Accounts Payable: Streamlines requests for quotation (RFQs), purchase orders, Goods Received Notes (RGN), landed cost apportionments, and automated 3-way invoice matching.
  5. Core Financial Ledger & Receivables: Posts financial journals, customer payments, credit balances, foreign currency revaluations, and trial balances without batch delays.
  6. Regulatory Compliance by Design: Native integration with Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) TIMS and eTIMS protocols, ensuring every invoice and credit note is cryptographically signed and QR-coded before dispatch.

---

2. Complete Module Directory

Guide 07Users, Roles & Access Governance/admin/usersStaff directory, branch bindings, role templates, atomic permissions, and contextual ABAC security policies.

---

3. End-to-End Implementation Project Lifecycle

When rolling out QSell for a new client organization, implementors must follow this strict 7-stage deployment sequence. Configuring modules out of order leads to blocked transactions and missing lookup dependencies.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Imp as Solutions Implementor
    participant Fnd as 1. Foundation & Legal Identity
    participant Str as 2. Locations, Tax & Numbers
    participant Mst as 3. Master Catalog & Pricing
    participant Log as 4. Delivery & Logistics
    participant Fin as 5. Finance & Postings
    participant Gov as 6. Users & Approvals
    participant Cut as 7. Cutover & Go-Live

    Imp->>Fnd: Configure Company Profile, Legal Name, KRA PIN, Bank Accounts & Brand Theme
    Imp->>Str: Set up Branches, Base Units of Measure, Tax Classifications & Number Series
    Imp->>Mst: Import Categories, Products, Kits, Customer Groups & Base Price Lists
    Imp->>Log: Define Delivery Zones, Rates, Dispatch Methods, Slots & Map Services
    Imp->>Fin: Set Chart of Accounts, Bank Accounts, Payment Providers & Posting Matrix
    Imp->>Gov: Define Staff Roles, Assign Branches, Configure Approval Chains & Thresholds
    Imp->>Cut: Perform Inventory Physical Count Cutover, Open Fiscal Period & Launch Pilot

Stage 1: Foundation & Legal Identity

  • Actions: Complete Company Profile (Guide 02), upload high-resolution logo, set legal trading name, register corporate KRA PIN, address, telephone, email, and primary bank details.
  • Verification: Preview invoice and receipt document layouts to ensure legal headers format correctly.

Stage 2: Locations, Tax & Numbering Series

  • Actions: Define physical operating branches (Guide 13). Configure Units of Measure (Guide 05). Map KRA Tax Classifications (16% General VAT, 0% Zero-rated, 8% Fuel, Exempt). Establish gapless Number Series for Orders, Invoices, Receipts, and POs.
  • Verification: Test number series generation to ensure sequence formatting matches company conventions (e.g., INV-2026-00001).

Stage 3: Master Catalog, Stock Locations & Pricing

  • Actions: Create stock locations (warehouses, shops, dispatch vehicles). Establish category trees. Import SKUs with barcodes, weights, and dimensions. Build Kits & Hampers. Establish Customer Groups (Retail, Wholesale, Trade). Build Price Lists with quantity breaks and minimum price floors (Guide 04).
  • Verification: Run the Price Check Simulator (/admin/pricing/check) on sample products to confirm margin floors and quantity discounts calculate properly.

Stage 4: Delivery Zones & Logistics Setup

  • Actions: Configure delivery zones using postal towns or map polygon boundaries (Guide 06). Configure rate cards (flat, weight-based, distance-based). Define delivery time slots and daily capacity caps. Connect courier APIs or create in-house rider profiles.
  • Verification: Enter a test address in checkout or counter order to verify the exact zone, fee, and delivery time slot are assigned.

Stage 5: Finance, Banking & Gateways

  • Actions: Set up Chart of Accounts (Guide 10). Configure General Ledger Posting Setup matrix. Set up commercial bank accounts and cash drawers (Guide 11). Integrate Safaricom M-Pesa Daraja APIs (Paybill/Till) and card payment gateways.
  • Verification: Execute a test KES 10.00 M-Pesa STK Push payment and confirm automatic transaction ledger recording and settlement allocation.

Stage 6: Users, Security & Approval Controls

  • Actions: Configure user accounts for staff members (Guide 07). Assign specific branches and roles (Cashier, Storekeeper, Dispatcher, Sales Rep, Accountant, Branch Manager). Build Approval Workflows (Guide 12) for high-value purchase orders, below-floor price overrides, and customer refunds.
  • Verification: Submit a purchase order exceeding a test user's signing limit and verify that the document halts in "Pending Approval" state and routes to the designated manager's inbox.

Stage 7: Cutover, Ledger Initialization & Go-Live

  • Actions: Lock legacy systems. Execute the Stock Ledger Cutover wizard (Guide 05), importing physical on-hand inventory balances location by location. Post opening customer debit balances and vendor accounts payable balances. Open the active fiscal period.
  • Verification: Print the Trial Balance and Stock Valuation reports and reconcile them to the client's certified opening balance sheet.

---

4. Sales Onboarding Curriculum (2-Week Mastery Track)

New commercial sales representatives and solutions consultants must complete this 10-day structured onboarding program to achieve fluency in pitching, demoing, and defending QSell against competing software.

Week 1: Core Commerce, Inventory & Logistics Operations

  • Day 1: Platform Vision & The Modern African Business Reality
  • Read: Guide 01 (Dashboard) and Guide 02 (Company Setup).
  • Key Topic: Why traditional international ERPs fail in East Africa (lack of native M-Pesa, complex KRA eTIMS integrations, poor road network support, lack of door cash reconciliation).
  • Practice: Configure a mock company profile, logo, and document layout in under 15 minutes.
  • Day 2: The Omnichannel Sales Journey & Order Blueprint
  • Read: Guide 03 (Sales & Orders).
  • Key Topic: Walk prospects through the journey from Web Storefront / Counter Order $\rightarrow$ Order Confirmed $\rightarrow$ Picking $\rightarrow$ Packing $\rightarrow$ Dispatched $\rightarrow$ Delivered.
  • Practice: Issue a proforma quote, email it to a prospect, convert it into a confirmed order, and explain the timestamped stage audit trail.
  • Day 3: Intelligent Pricing, Margin Protection & Promotions
  • Read: Guide 04 (Pricing Engine).
  • Key Topic: How QSell eliminates rogue discounting and protects operating margins using price floors and role-based override limits.
  • Practice: Use the Price Check Simulator to explain a complex pricing waterfall (Customer Group + Quantity Break + Active Promo Code - Margin Floor Lock).
  • Day 4: Inventory Control, Multi-Location WMS & Stock Integrity
  • Read: Guide 05 (Products & Inventory).
  • Key Topic: How QSell stops inventory theft and phantom stockouts across multiple branches and mobile vans.
  • Practice: Execute a stock transfer from Central Warehouse to a Van, demonstrate in-transit tracking, and conduct a cycle count that continues while cashiers sell.
  • Day 5: Delivery Logistics, Dispatch & Cash on Delivery (COD)
  • Read: Guide 06 (Delivery) and Guide 14 (Rider Portal).
  • Key Topic: How QSell solves the last-mile delivery nightmare: pin-on-map zoning, rider run sheets, doorstep PIN verification, and door payment reconciliation.
  • Practice: Plan a 3-stop delivery run on the Dispatch Board, open the Rider Mobile App, complete a dropoff, and reconcile cash collected at the counter.

Week 2: Procurement, Finance, Compliance & Executive Pitching

  • Day 6: Vendor Management & 3-Way Match Procurement
  • Read: Guide 09 (Vendor Management).
  • Key Topic: Preventing procurement fraud through public RFQ bidding, Purchase Order approvals, Goods Received Notes (RGN), and automated 3-way matching.
  • Practice: Issue an RFQ, submit a vendor bid through the Vendor Portal, generate a Purchase Order, receive partial goods, and book the supplier invoice.
  • Day 7: Double-Entry Financial Accounting & Receivables
  • Read: Guide 10 (Finance & AR) and Guide 11 (Banking & Payments).
  • Key Topic: Why CFOs love QSell: real-time general ledger postings, automated sales/stock sync, customer store credit wallets, and bank CSV reconciliation.
  • Practice: Post a general journal, receive a customer payment, allocate it across three invoices, and inspect the real-time Trial Balance.
  • Day 8: Regulatory Compliance: KRA eTIMS & Tax Architecture
  • Read: Guide 13 (Settings & KRA eTIMS).
  • Key Topic: Turning KRA compliance into a sales superpower: zero external fiscal boxes required, automated digital invoice signing, and item synchronization.
  • Practice: Explain the difference between TIMS (hardware device) and eTIMS (cloud digital signing) and demonstrate how an invoice receives its cryptographic signature.
  • Day 9: Governance, Approvals & Enterprise Access Control
  • Read: Guide 07 (Users & Roles) and Guide 12 (Approvals).
  • Key Topic: Corporate governance: separation of duties, tiered financial limits, substitute approvers during leave, and complete audit trail.
  • Practice: Configure an approval rule for orders over KES 100,000, trigger an approval request, reject with a reason, and show the audit trail.
  • Day 10: The Master Executive Pitch & Competitive Objections
  • Read: Guide 08 (Projects) and review all Value Proposition sections.
  • Key Topic: Delivering the 30-minute C-suite pitch to a CEO and CFO; handling objections regarding data migration, staff training, and software reliability.
  • Final Exercise: Deliver a full end-to-end platform demo and answer 5 live prospect objections.

chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 01: Business Overview & Dashboard (/admin)

The Business Overview dashboard is the operational and financial cockpit of QSell. It aggregates company-wide commercial performance in real time across all sales channels, retail branches, warehouse locations, and payment gateways.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Blind Operations: Traditional businesses wait until the end of the day or month for accountants to balance physical receipt books and compile spreadsheets, leaving management blind to intraday inventory shortages or slumping sales.
  • Disconnected Branch Visibility: Multi-location retail and wholesale operations struggle to compare branch performance fairly, resulting in slow-moving stock trapped in one branch while another suffers stockouts.
  • Unreconciled Cash Leakage: Sales numbers often disguise collection failures. A company may show KES 1,000,000 in sales on paper, but only KES 400,000 in actual bank deposits, with the balance lost to uncollected credit or delayed mobile-money settlements.
  • Invisible Margins: Heavy discounting by sales staff often inflates top-line revenue while wiping out bottom-line profit.

Target Client Profiles

  • Multi-Branch Retail Chains: Supermarkets, electronics stores, and clothing boutiques needing centralized branch rankings and till balances.
  • High-Velocity Wholesalers & FMCG Distributors: Businesses needing real-time dispatch velocities, receivables ageing, and payment method breakdowns.
  • Executive Directors & C-Suite: CEOs and CFOs requiring instant access to true gross margin, tax collected, and critical items requiring attention.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you never have to ask your store managers for an end-of-day sales report. The moment an order is punched into a till in Kisumu or checked out on your Nairobi website, your executive dashboard updates instantly. You see not just your total revenue, but the exact cash and M-Pesa collected, your true realized profit margin after product costs, and which specific branch or product is driving your growth today."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% Intraday Telemetry: Zero reporting delay between order placement and executive awareness.
  • Direct Collection Audit: Instantly compares Total Sales vs. Money Collected, exposing payment collection deficits before they turn into bad debts.
  • Realized Margin Tracking: Monitors gross margin percentage in real time, alerting management when discounts erode product profitability.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

Before the Business Overview dashboard can display complete figures, the following foundational setup must be completed:

graph TD
    B[1. Operating Branches Configured] --> P[2. Products & Landed Cost Defined]
    P --> G[3. Payment Providers Connected]
    G --> U[4. User Account Assigned to Branch/Scope]
    U --> DASH[Dashboard Populates Metrics]
  1. Operating Branches: At least one branch must be active under Settings > Branches.
  2. Product Cost Prices: Products must have their unit purchase cost entered under Catalog > Products for the Gross Profit KPI to calculate.
  3. Payment Gateways: At least one payment provider (M-Pesa, Cash Till, Bank, or Card) must be configured under Settings > Payments.
  4. Staff Scope & Permissions:
  • The user must possess the dashboard:read permission.
  • The user must be assigned to either a specific branch (to see localized data) or granted company-wide access (to see consolidated data and the branch filter).

---

3. Module Architecture & Telemetry Data Flow

The dashboard dynamically queries multiple operational domains in parallel and calculates real-time comparisons:

graph LR
    subgraph Transactions["Operational Ingestion"]
        ORD[Sales Orders Placed]
        PAY[Payment Gateways Confirmed]
        DEL[Delivery Statuses]
        STK[Inventory Thresholds]
    end

    subgraph Aggregator["Reporting Engine"]
        PERIOD[Date Period & Comparison Calculator]
        SCOPE[Branch Security & Currency Filter]
        FLOW[Order Flow Classifier]
    end

    subgraph DashboardView["Executive Presentation"]
        CARDS[KPI Cards & Sparklines]
        CHART[Trend Charts vs Previous Period]
        BRANCH[Branch Ranking Table]
        ATTN[Actionable Attention Queue]
    end

    Transactions --> Aggregator
    Aggregator --> DashboardView
  • Scope Boundary: If a staff member is assigned to the "Mombasa Branch", the system automatically restricts all queries to orders, payments, and stock originating from that branch.
  • Currency Isolation: All values are reported in the company's Base Currency (e.g., KES). Transactions placed in secondary foreign currencies (USD, EUR) are flagged in an informational footnote with order counts.

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

The Dashboard consists of five integrated functional sections:

Section A: Top Filter & Date Range Bar

  • Preset Period Selector: Quick-jump dropdown for rapid temporal slicing.
  • Comparison Mode Selector: Configures the comparative baseline against which percentage growth/decline is measured.
  • Branch Scope Selector: Dropdown to switch between company-wide consolidation or a specific branch.
  • Last Updated & Refresh Indicator: Displays the exact timestamp the data was pulled and the active timezone (e.g., Africa/Nairobi).

Section B: Executive Headline & Attention Banner

  • Headline Summary: Natural-language sentences summarizing current performance (e.g., "Sales are up 14% compared to the previous 30 days, driven by Central Store.").
  • Attention Queue (AttentionList): Visual callout cards for items requiring immediate human intervention:
  • Unpaid Orders Pending Delivery
  • Failed or Timed-Out Gateway Payments
  • Low Stock / Depleted SKUs
  • Late Delivery SLA Breaches

Section C: Sales Performance & Order Flow (Card: Sales)

  • Key Metric Tiles:
  • Sales: Total gross revenue from valid orders placed in the selected period.
  • Orders: Total number of qualifying orders.
  • Average Order Value (AOV): Gross Sales divided by Order Count.
  • Tax Included in Sales: Total VAT and consumption taxes included in the reported sales total.
  • Revenue Trend Chart: Daily or hourly sales graph plotting the current period's velocity against the comparative prior period.
  • Order Flow Breakdown: Visual status bar and breakdown table showing where placed orders ended up:
  • Counted in Sales: Completed, In-Transit, Awaiting Fulfillment, Credit Sales.
  • Excluded from Sales: Abandoned Checkouts, Cancelled by Customer, Payment Failed, Refunded.
  • Sales by Branch Table: Multi-column comparison listing Branch Name, Revenue, Revenue Share %, Total Orders, and Growth % vs. Prior Period.
  • Best Sellers Ranking: Top products by revenue, showing units sold and gross income.

Section D: Money Collected & Liquidity (Card: Money Collected)

  • Collected Revenue: Total cleared funds received through payment gateways and cash registers.
  • Collection Rate %: (Money Collected ÷ Gross Sales) × 100.
  • Note: Can exceed 100% when credit customers settle invoices from previous months.
  • In-Flight & Failed Payment Audit: Flags customer transactions currently processing vs. abandoned.
  • Payment Method Distribution: Metered progress bars showing the percentage and shilling value collected via M-Pesa Paybill, Cash Till, Bank Transfer, and Credit Cards.
  • Non-Cash Tenders Notice: Footnote disclosing value paid via Loyalty Points redemptions and Gift Cards.

Section E: Gross Profit & Margin Control (Card: Gross Profit)

  • Gross Profit (KES): Realized profit calculated as Selling Price - Unit Cost Price.
  • Gross Margin %: (Gross Profit ÷ Gross Sales) × 100.
  • Uncosted Items Notice: Warns if products without an entered cost were sold, preventing distorted margin figures.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

Control / MetricTypePurposeValidation & Rules
Period PresetDropdownSets the time window for all metrics.Options: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, This Month, Last Month, Custom.
Compare ModeDropdownDetermines the comparison baseline.Options: Previous Period (same duration immediately preceding), Previous Year (same dates last year).
Branch ScopeDropdownFilters metrics to a specific operational unit.Disabled if the logged-in user lacks multi-branch view rights. Shows "All Branches" or specific branch names.
From DateDate InputCustom period start date.Format YYYY-MM-DD. Must be earlier than or equal to To Date.
To DateDate InputCustom period end date.Format YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be a future date beyond current server time.
Sales KPICurrencyGross monetary value of valid orders.Formatted in base currency (KES) with thousands separators. Excludes cancelled and refunded orders.
Collection RatePercentageRatio of cash received to sales booked.Displayed to 1 decimal place. Highlights liquidity health.
Gross MarginPercentageOperating profitability ratio.Color-coded: Green for healthy margins, Amber for marginal, Red for negative gross profit.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Analyzing Today's Intraday Performance

  1. Navigate to /admin in the sidebar.
  2. Locate the Period dropdown in the top filter bar.
  3. Click the dropdown and select Today.
  4. The screen refreshes without full page reload.
  5. Review the Sales tile to see today's revenue generated since 00:00.
  6. Check the Money Collected tile to verify that cash/M-Pesa deposits match order revenue.
  7. Click any item in the Attention Queue (e.g., "3 orders pending dispatch") to jump directly to the pre-filtered order processing screen.

Action 2: Comparing Branch Sales for Monthly Review

  1. In the top filter bar, set Period to This Month.
  2. Set Compare to Previous Period (or Previous Year for seasonal analysis).
  3. Scroll down to the Sales by branch table.
  4. Review the Share % column to identify your highest-volume branch.
  5. Review the vs Previous Period column:
  • Positive numbers indicate revenue growth.
  • Negative numbers indicate underperformance requiring operational review.
  1. Click the Branch dropdown in the top filter bar and select the specific underperforming branch to isolate its top sellers and order bottlenecks.

Action 3: Reviewing Payment Method Health & Failed Transactions

  1. Locate the Money collected card.
  2. Inspect the In-Flight & Failed Payments status banner.
  3. If failed payment attempts are flagged, note the count.
  4. Review the breakdown list of payment methods:
  • Identify whether M-Pesa Paybill or In-Store Cash represents the primary liquidity source.
  • Note any funds flagged under "unconfigured methods" (payments received on legacy tills no longer assigned to branches).

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

Order Qualification Rules (What Counts as a Sale?)

  • Counted in Sales:
  • Orders marked as Completed, Delivered, Dispatched, Processing, or Confirmed.
  • Credit sales with approved payment terms (invoiced to customer account).
  • Excluded from Sales:
  • Abandoned online shopping carts where the customer exited before checkout.
  • Payment attempts that returned Failed, Cancelled, or Expired from Safaricom or card processors.
  • Orders formally cancelled or refunded.

Multi-Branch Permission Boundary

  • If a user has branches:read and dashboard:read across the company, they see consolidated numbers and can toggle between branches.
  • If a user is restricted to a single branch (e.g. "Westlands Branch"), the branch dropdown is locked, and the byBranch comparison table is hidden to prevent competitive data leakage among branch staff.

Zero-Activity State Handling

  • If a newly launched shop or branch has zero orders in the selected period, the dashboard displays:
  • A clean empty state: "No orders were placed in this period."
  • A dynamic jump button: "Show the 30 days up to [Last Order Date]" allowing managers to quickly review the last active sales period without guessing dates.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

StepVerification TaskExpected ResultPass/Fail
1Create a test branch and assign products to it.Branch appears in the dashboard branch filter dropdown.[ ]
2Place a test order for KES 5,000 using M-Pesa.Sales KPI increases by KES 5,000; Orders KPI increments by 1.[ ]
3Confirm M-Pesa payment reception.Money Collected tile updates by KES 5,000; Collection Rate reflects 100%.[ ]
4Log in as a Branch-Restricted Cashier.Dashboard only shows data for the cashier's assigned branch.[ ]
5Verify Gross Margin calculation.Product cost is subtracted from KES 5,000; accurate gross margin % is displayed.[ ]

Guide 02: Company Setup & Storefront Identity (/admin/company)

The Company Setup module establishes the legal, fiscal, operational, and visual identity of the business. It governs how the company presents itself to customers on the web storefront and how legal identity, tax information, and banking instructions appear on formal commercial documents (quotes, invoices, and receipts).

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Inconsistent Branding Across Channels: Businesses frequently struggle with fragmented brand images—a web shop that looks different from printed counter receipts, and quotes that lack professional banking instructions.
  • KRA Tax Invoicing Compliance Risks: Failing to display an exact legal name, physical address, and KRA PIN on invoices invalidates customer input tax deductions and incurs penalties from the Kenya Revenue Authority.
  • Costly Custom Development for Simple Storefront Changes: Minor changes like changing a brand accent color, updating a customer service WhatsApp number, or posting a temporary delivery banner usually require hiring external web developers.

Target Client Profiles

  • Branded Consumer Retailers & E-Commerce Merchants: Businesses requiring an online storefront that mirrors their physical store branding and corporate identity.
  • B2B Suppliers & Corporate Wholesalers: Organizations issuing proforma quotations and credit invoices requiring legal terms, VAT registration numbers, and wire transfer bank details.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you can launch a fully branded, legally compliant online store and ERP in minutes. You don't need a web developer to change your brand colors, update your customer service hotline, or customize your invoice footer notes. Enter your details once in the Company Setup module, and every quote, invoice, receipt, and web page instantly updates with your brand, your KRA PIN, and your direct bank details."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Zero Developer Fees for Brand & Storefront Management: 100% no-code configuration of colors, grid density, banners, FAQs, and policies.
  • 100% Tax Document Legality: Guarantees that every printed and emailed invoice satisfies Section 23 of the Kenyan Tax Procedures Act.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

Company Setup is the Stage 1 Foundation of the entire QSell platform. It should be configured before adding products, creating users, or transacting.

graph TD
    P[1. Company Profile: Legal Name & KRA PIN] --> D[2. Document Layouts: Headers & Footers]
    D --> A[3. Appearance: Brand Colors & Density]
    A --> S[4. Support & Contacts: WhatsApp & FAQs]
    S --> B[5. Banners & Policies: Terms & Notices]
    B --> M[6. Module Renaming: Custom Labels]
  • Required Staff Permission: Users must possess the company:read permission to view and company:write (or administrative role) to save changes.

---

  5. In the Address & location section, enter the physical street address, city, and county.
  6. In the Banking section, enter the bank name and account number where customer wire transfers should be directed.

  • Must end with a single alphabetic letter.
  • If an invalid PIN is entered (e.g. 12345678 or P05123456), the save action is rejected with the message: "KRA PIN must be a letter (A or P), nine digits and a letter."

Document Sizing and Print Ratios

  • Uploaded logos are automatically resized on invoices to maintain a maximum height of 60px and maximum width of 240px, preventing document pagination overflow.
  • If no logo is uploaded, the document header gracefully falls back to displaying the Trading Name in bold 18pt typography.

Guide 03: Sales Quotes & Customer Orders (/admin/sales)

The Sales & Fulfillment module orchestrates the complete Order-to-Cash (O2C) lifecycle. It manages proforma sales quotations, omnichannel customer orders (online storefront, physical point-of-sale, and back-office credit sales), customer master cards, credit limit enforcement, newsletter subscribers, and product reviews.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The Delivery & Fulfillment Blame Game: When an order is delivered late or items go missing, sales reps blame the warehouse, warehouse staff blame the dispatcher, and dispatchers blame the courier. QSell eliminates this through an immutable, server-timestamped order timeline that tracks the exact second an order entered and exited every stage (Received $\rightarrow$ Confirmed $\rightarrow$ Reserved $\rightarrow$ Picked $\rightarrow$ Packed $\rightarrow$ Dispatched $\rightarrow$ Delivered).
  • Uncontrolled Credit Overextension: Sales reps often accept orders from customers who have exceeded their credit limits or have 90-day overdue invoices. QSell enforces hard credit limit checks at order placement, automatically blocking unapproved credit orders.
  • Friction in B2B Quotation Negotiations: B2B deals require multi-line formal proforma quotes with negotiated discounts and validity dates. In manual systems, quotes are made on spreadsheets and must be re-typed into the accounting system when won. QSell converts quotes to confirmed sales orders in a single click with zero data re-entry.

Target Client Profiles

  • Wholesalers & B2B Trade Distributors: Managing formal quotations, corporate customer accounts, credit terms (Net 30, Net 60), and multi-branch delivery schedules.
  • Omnichannel Retailers: Processing walk-in counter sales alongside high-volume e-commerce orders.
  • Field Sales Teams: Generating field quotes on tablets that link directly to warehouse inventory.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, your sales team moves deals from quotation to cash with zero friction and 100% accountability. Every quote you generate can be converted into a live sales order with a single click. Every single order is tracked with an unalterable server timestamp at every milestone—so you know exactly how long an order took to be picked in the warehouse, when it was handed to the rider, and the exact second the customer signed for it at the door."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Zero Double-Entry Overhead: Quotes instantly convert to Orders, Orders to Packing Slips, and Orders to KRA-signed Invoices.
  • Elimination of Bad Debts: Automatic credit-ceiling enforcement blocks orders when customers exceed agreed limits.
  • Order SLA Enforcement: Real-time alerts when orders languish in picking or packing beyond target thresholds.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    PROD[1. Products & Selling Prices Active] --> CUST[2. Customer Master Cards & Groups]
    CUST --> NUM[3. Number Series Bound: Quotes & Orders]
    NUM --> SLA[4. Order Stage Target Timers Set]
    SLA --> SALES[Sales Quotes & Orders Active]
  1. Active Sellable Products: Products must be assigned a business classification marked as "Sold to Customers" with active selling prices.
  2. Customer Master Cards: Cash or credit customer accounts must exist under /admin/customers.
  3. Number Series: Document number series for Sales Quotes (QT-) and Sales Orders (ORD-) must be active under Settings > Number Series.
  4. Order SLA Targets: Stage timeout targets should be defined under Settings > Order Targets to trigger late-stage notifications.
  5. Staff Permissions:
  • quotes:read, quotes:manage: Access and manage quotations.
  • orders:read, orders:manage: Process orders and print packing slips.
  • customers:read, customers:manage: Create and edit customer cards.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Sales module coordinates five operational areas:

graph LR
    subgraph SalesSubModules["Sales Sub-Modules"]

        O["Customer Orders\n(/admin/orders)"]

    end

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Sub-Module 1: Sales Quotes (/admin/quotes)

  • Quotes List View (QuotesTable): Paged table showing Quote Number, Customer Name, Issue Date, Expiration Date, Total Amount, and Status (Draft, Sent, Accepted, Converted, Expired, Rejected).
  • Quote Creation & Editor (QuoteEditor):
  • Customer selection with instant customer credit standing preview.
  • Line-item editor: SKU selection, unit of measure, quantity, base price, discount %, and tax rate.
  • Real-time calculation toolbar: Subtotal, total discount, VAT, and grand total.
  • Validity expiration date picker and customer memo notes.
  • Quote Detail Modal (QuoteDetails): Full proforma document view with actions to Print PDF, Send via Email, Accept, or Convert to Order.

Sub-Module 2: Customer Orders (/admin/orders)

  • Orders List View: Filterable by Channel (Web Shop, Counter POS, Sales Rep, B2B Account), Status (Pending, Confirmed, Processing, Dispatched, Delivered, Cancelled), Payment Status (Unpaid, Paid, Partial), and Branch.
  • Order Details Modal (OrderDetailsModal): Comprehensive multi-tab operational hub:
  1. Order Summary Tab: Order lines, quantities, unit prices, applied coupons, delivery fees, and grand total.
  2. Stage Timeline Panel (OrderTimelinePanel): Visual vertical timeline showing every stage event with exact server timestamps, actors, and duration spent in each stage.
  3. Deliveries Panel (OrderDeliveriesPanel): Shows partial and complete dispatches, courier tracking numbers, and delivery run links.
  4. Stock Allocation Panel (OrderStockPanel): Shows warehouse reservations, batches allocated, and goods issue status.
  5. Collection Panel (OrderCollectionPanel): Payment method, gateway reference, M-Pesa receipt code, and door cash collection status.
  6. KRA Invoice Preview (OrderInvoicePreview): Electronic tax invoice details, KRA digital signature code, and QR verification code.

Sub-Module 3: Customers (/admin/customers)

  • Customer Directory: Tabular list showing Account Code, Customer Name, Account Type (Cash or Credit), Phone, Email, City, Balance Owed, and Status (Active, Suspended).
  • Customer Card Details:
  • Identity & Legal: Name, Trading Name, KRA PIN, Identity Document (National ID / Passport / Incorporation Cert).
  • Credit Terms & Risk: Credit limit (e.g. KES 500,000), payment grace period (e.g. 30 days), and price group assignment (e.g. Wholesale Tier 1).
  • Billing & Shipping Addresses: Multiple physical delivery locations with geo-coordinates.
  • Dimension Bindings (DimensionFields): Cost center, sales territory, or industry vertical tags for financial reporting.

Sub-Module 4: Newsletter (/admin/newsletter)

  • List of customer email subscribers captured via storefront footers and popups.
  • Export to CSV action for email marketing campaigns (Mailchimp, Sendgrid).

Sub-Module 5: Product Reviews (/admin/reviews)

  • Customer review moderation queue showing Product Name, Customer Name, Star Rating (1-5), Review Headline, Review Body, and Submission Date.
  • Action buttons: Approve Review (publishes to storefront) or Reject / Archive (removes from public display).

---

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Creating and Converting a Proforma Sales Quote to an Order

  1. Navigate to /admin/quotes and click New Quote in the top right.
  2. In the Customer lookup field, search for and select the client (e.g. "Acme Construction Ltd").
  3. Set the Valid Until date (e.g., 14 days from today).
  4. Click Add Line Item.
  5. In the product autocomplete, select the product (e.g., "500W Solar Panel").
  6. Enter the Quantity (e.g. 20). The system automatically pulls the current customer group price.
  7. Enter a negotiated discount (e.g. 5%). The system recalculates the subtotal and VAT in real time.
  8. Click Save Quote. The quote status becomes Sent.
  9. When the client approves the proposal, open the quote details and click the Convert to Order button.
  10. An InlineConfirm prompt appears: "Convert Quote #QT-00142 into a confirmed Sales Order?"
  11. Click Confirm Conversion.
  12. The quote status updates to Converted, and the system redirects to the newly created Sales Order with all lines, prices, and customer details intact.

Action 2: Inspecting an Order's Timestamped Stage Timeline

  1. Navigate to /admin/orders.
  2. Locate the order using the search bar (by Order Number, Customer Name, or Phone).
  3. Click the order row to open the Order Details Modal.
  4. Click the Timeline tab.
  5. The timeline renders chronologically:
  • 09:14:02 — Order Placed (Channel: Web Shop, Actor: Customer).
  • 09:14:05 — Payment Confirmed (M-Pesa STK Push: KES 14,500, Ref: QA712XYZ).
  • 09:15:20 — Stock Reserved (Warehouse: Central Depot, 2 items locked).
  • 09:40:12 — Pick Started (Actor: John Kamau - Storekeeper).
  • 09:52:00 — Packed & Ready for Dispatch (Packing Slip #PS-1082 printed).
  • 10:15:30 — Dispatched (Rider: Peter Ochieng, Run #RUN-04).
  • 10:48:15 — Delivered (Customer Signature & Verification PIN Confirmed).
  1. Hover over any stage to view duration spent (e.g., "Time in Packing: 11 minutes").

Action 3: Reviewing and Moderating Customer Product Reviews

  1. Navigate to /admin/reviews.
  2. The table displays pending reviews submitted by shoppers on the storefront.
  3. Review the star rating, title, and comments.
  4. To approve: Click Approve. The review immediately becomes visible on the product page and updates the product's aggregate star rating.
  5. To reject: Click Reject. An inline text prompt asks for an internal reason (e.g., "Offensive language" or "Spam"). Click Confirm Rejection.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

The Credit Limit Breach Rule

  • When an order is placed on credit (either via counter order or quote conversion), the system checks:

$$\text{Current Unpaid Balance} + \text{New Order Total} \le \text{Customer Credit Limit}$$

  • If the calculation exceeds the limit:
  • If an Approval Workflow for credit override is configured, the order status halts in Pending Credit Approval and alerts the Credit Manager.
  • If no approval workflow exists, order creation is blocked with the error: "Customer credit limit exceeded by KES [Amount]. Payment required before placement."

Stage Immutability & Reversals

  • Once an order stage timestamp is recorded in the append-only event log, it can never be edited or deleted.
  • If an order must be cancelled after dispatch:
  1. The order status moves to Delivery Failed or Cancelled.
  2. A return-to-stock movement is issued, recording the physical return of the goods to inventory.
  3. A credit note is generated referencing the original invoice.

---

2Issue a Sales Quote with a 10% line discount.Proforma calculates discount and VAT accurately; status shows Draft/Sent.[ ]

Guide 04: Pricing Engine, Promotions & Margins (/admin/pricing)

The Pricing Engine is the commercial brain of QSell. It governs how base prices are determined across different customer tiers, retail channels, and branches, while enforcing strict margin protection rules, promotional coupons, retrospective rebates, loyalty points, and role-based discount caps.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Erosion of Profitability Through Uncontrolled Discounting: In competitive sales environments, sales reps frequently offer deep discounts to close deals, inadvertently selling products below cost or wiping out gross margin.
  • Accidental Discount Stacking: Businesses often run promotional coupons (e.g. 10% off) that unintentionally stack on top of existing wholesale volume discounts and loyalty redemptions, leading to crippling margin loss.
  • Complexity in Multi-Tier B2B Pricing: Managing different price sheets for retail customers, wholesale stockists, contractors, and export clients on paper or spreadsheets causes billing errors and client disputes.
  • No Explanation of How a Price Was Reached: When a customer asks "Why was I charged KES 1,850 instead of KES 1,700?", legacy ERPs cannot explain the calculation. QSell generates a deterministic Price Trace explaining every step in the waterfall.

Target Client Profiles

  • Wholesalers & FMCG Distributors: Utilizing customer tiers (Wholesale A/B/C), minimum order quantities (MOQs), and tiered volume breaks (e.g. 1-10 units @ KES 1,000; 11-50 units @ KES 920; 51+ units @ KES 850).
  • Multi-Branch Retailers: Charging localized prices based on branch geography or transport costs (e.g. Nairobi vs. Lodwar).
  • High-Margin Hardware & Contractor Suppliers: Requiring cost-plus minimum price floors to ensure every sale yields at least a 15% gross margin.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you will never accidentally sell a product at a loss again. Our pricing engine lets you configure sophisticated wholesale price lists, volume breaks, and seasonal promotional codes, while locking your bottom line with automated Price Floors. If a salesperson attempts to discount an item below your required margin floor, the system blocks the transaction or automatically routes it to the Managing Director for approval. Best of all, our Price Check simulator allows you to test any pricing rule before it goes live."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% Margin Floor Lock: Hard stop prevents any quote or order from being sold below cost + minimum markup.
  • Deterministic Price Trace: Complete auditability on every transaction line item.
  • Controlled Discretionary Limits: Sales reps, supervisors, and managers each have defined discount authority ceilings.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    PROD[1. Products & Base Landed Costs Configured] --> GRP[2. Customer Groups Defined: Wholesale, Retail]
    GRP --> LIST[3. Price Lists Created with Scope & Validity]
    LIST --> FLOOR[4. Price Floors Set: Cost + Minimum %]
    FLOOR --> LIMIT[5. Staff Override Limits Assigned]
    LIMIT --> SIM[6. Price Check Simulator Verification]
  1. Product Master Data: SKUs must exist with valid Base Selling Prices and Unit Cost Prices under Catalog > Products.
  2. Customer Groups: Defined under /admin/pricing/groups (e.g. Retail Cash, Trade Tier 1, Government Tender).
  3. Price Lists: Created with currency (KES), validity dates, and branch/customer scope.
  4. Price Floors: Configured under /admin/pricing/floors to set non-negotiable minimum profit barriers.
  5. Override Limits: Configured under /admin/pricing/limits to set role-based discount authority.
  6. Required Permissions: pricing:read to view and pricing:manage to create or alter price rules.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Pricing Engine operates as a deterministic 2-phase calculation waterfall:

graph TD
    subgraph Phase1["Phase 1: Base Price Resolution (Choose Winner)"]
        IN[Inputs: Customer, Group, Branch, SKU, Qty, Date]
        IN --> MATCH[Match Active Price Sources]
        MATCH --> RANK[Rank by Specificity: Customer > Group > Branch > Standard]
        RANK --> PRIO[Break Ties: Priority > Newest Effective Date]
        PRIO --> BASE[Base Price Chosen]
    end

    subgraph Phase2["Phase 2: Adjustments & Safeguards (Stack & Check)"]
        BASE --> DISC[Apply Eligible Discounts & Coupons]
        DISC --> REB[Accrue Retrospective Rebates]
        REB --> PROMO[Evaluate Loyalty Points & Gift Cards]
        PROMO --> FLOOR{Check Price Floor: Price >= Cost + Min Margin?}
        FLOOR -- "Compliant" --> WIN[Effective Final Price]
        FLOOR -- "Breached" --> APP{Within Staff Override Limit?}
        APP -- "Yes" --> WARN[Flag Margin Warning & Allow]
        APP -- "No" --> BLOCK[Route to Approval / Block Sale]
    end

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Sub-Module 1: Customer Groups (/admin/pricing/groups)

  • Defines customer segmentation tiers (e.g., Walk-in Retail, Wholesale Bronze, Wholesale Platinum, Staff).
  • Allows assigning customers in bulk or binding automatic qualifying criteria.

Sub-Module 2: Price Lists (/admin/pricing)

  • Table of active and scheduled price lists showing Code, Name, Currency, Priority, Effective Dates, and Scope.
  • Line Editor: Set prices per SKU, Unit of Measure, and Quantity Breaks (e.g. Buy 10+, Buy 50+, Buy 100+).

Sub-Module 3: Discounts & Coupons (/admin/pricing/discounts)

  • Configures promotional campaigns:
  • Type: Percentage discount (e.g. 10% off), Fixed amount (e.g. KES 500 off), or Free Item.
  • Trigger: Coupon code entry, minimum cart value threshold (e.g. Spend KES 10,000+), or specific product bundles.
  • Stacking Rules: Whether this discount can combine with other active promotions.

Sub-Module 4: Rebates (/admin/pricing/rebates)

  • Long-term customer loyalty agreements:
  • Tracks cumulative purchase volume over a calendar quarter or year.
  • Accrues rebate percentages (e.g. "Buy KES 2,000,000 of cement in Q1, receive 3% credit rebate").
  • Automatically generates Accounts Receivable Credit Memos upon milestone attainment.

Sub-Module 5: Loyalty Points (/admin/pricing/loyalty)

  • Point accrual engine: Set earn rate (e.g. 1 Point per KES 100 spent) and redemption rate (e.g. 1 Point = KES 1.00 store credit).
  • Expiration rules and minimum points required to redeem.

Sub-Module 6: Gift Cards (/admin/pricing/gift-cards)

  • Prepaid voucher management: Generate digital gift card codes, assign balances, track partial redemptions, and monitor expiration dates.

Sub-Module 7: Price Book (/admin/pricing/book)

  • Printable and exportable matrix showing what every product sells for in any combination of Customer Group, Branch, and Quantity tier. Ideal for distributing physical price sheets to field sales agents.

Sub-Module 8: Pricing Insights (/admin/pricing/insights)

  • Executive analytics dashboard displaying:
  • Average realized gross margin across all orders.
  • Total revenue surrendered to promotional discounts and coupon codes.
  • Frequency of manual price overrides by sales representatives.

Sub-Module 9: Price Floors (/admin/pricing/floors)

  • The ultimate margin defense system:
  • Configures minimum selling prices based on:
  • Cost + Percentage Markup (e.g. Cost + 15%).
  • Cost + Fixed Amount (e.g. Cost + KES 200).
  • Hard Absolute Price Floor (e.g. Never sell below KES 1,500).
  • Scoped by specific Product, Product Group, or Category.

Sub-Module 10: Override Limits (/admin/pricing/limits)

  • Governs how far a staff member may manually lower a price or apply a discretionary discount:
  • Junior Sales Rep: Max 3% discount, cannot breach price floor.
  • Senior Sales Account Manager: Max 10% discount.
  • Branch Manager: Max 18% discount.
  • Commercial Director: Unlimited override authority.

Sub-Module 11: Price Check / Simulator (/admin/pricing/check)

  • The interactive sandbox where implementors and sales reps can test pricing scenarios:
  • Input: Select a Customer, Branch, Product SKU, Quantity, and Date.
  • Output: Instant live calculation with full waterfall trace displaying every considered price list, why one won, and which discounts applied.

Sub-Module 12: Price Rules (/admin/pricing/rules)

  • Master resolution settings configuring the relative weights and specificity rankings of competing price sources.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Setting Up a Tiered Wholesale Price List

  1. Navigate to /admin/pricing and click New Price List.
  2. Enter List Name: "Wholesale Platinum Tier 1".
  3. Set Currency: KES.
  4. Set Scope: In the Customer Group dropdown, select "Wholesale Platinum".
  5. Set Priority: 10 (higher priority wins over generic lists).
  6. Click Save & Add Products.
  7. In the product lines table, click Add Product.
  8. Select the SKU (e.g., "Cement 50kg Bag").
  9. In Tier 1: Set From Qty: 1, Price: 750.00.
  10. Click Add Tier: Set From Qty: 50, Price: 710.00.
  11. Click Add Tier: Set From Qty: 200, Price: 680.00.
  12. Click Save Price List.
  13. Status updates to Active. Any Wholesale Platinum customer ordering 50+ bags instantly receives KES 710.00.

Action 2: Protecting Margins by Configuring a Price Floor

  1. Navigate to /admin/pricing/floors and click New Price Floor.
  2. Set Scope Type to Category.
  3. Select Category: "Power Tools & Machinery".
  4. Set Floor Method: Cost + Markup %.
  5. Enter Floor Value: 20.0 (meaning Cost + 20%).
  6. Set Enforcement: Hard Stop (Block Sale).
  7. Click Activate Price Floor.
  8. A green confirmation banner displays: "Price floor activated. 48 products protected." Any attempt to sell a power tool below cost + 20% is now impossible across all channels.

Action 3: Simulating a Transaction in the Price Check Sandbox

  1. Navigate to /admin/pricing/check.
  2. In the Customer lookup, select "QuickFix Contractors".
  3. In the Product lookup, select "Inverter 5kVA".
  4. In the Quantity box, type 5.
  5. In the Branch dropdown, select "Nairobi Westlands".
  6. Click the Simulate Price button.
  7. The Waterfall Trace displays:
  • Standard Retail Price: KES 120,000.00
  • Customer Group Match (Trade): KES 108,000.00 (Wins by Specificity)
  • Quantity Break (5+ units): KES 102,000.00
  • Active Coupon SAVE5: - KES 5,100.00 (Applied)
  • Price Floor Check: Landed Cost KES 85,000.00 + 15% Floor (KES 97,750.00).
  • Floor Result: PASS (Net KES 96,900 is below floor? Triggers warning/approval).
  1. The tool displays the exact formula and reason string that will be written to the order.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

Specificity Hierarchy (Who Wins When Prices Compete?)

When multiple active price sources match an order line, the winner is determined strictly by the Specificity Hierarchy:

  1. Contract Locked Price (Explicit legal agreement with client).
  2. Customer-Specific Price (Negotiated price sheet for this single account).
  3. Customer Group Price (Tiered wholesale or trade group).
  4. Route / Van Price (Mobile distribution route).
  5. Branch / Location Price (Regional store price).
  6. Standard Product Price (Base catalog price).

Ties are broken by Price List Priority integer, then Newest Effective Date.

Preventing Coupon Cannibalization

  • If a discount has the flag allow_stacking = false, applying it disables all other promotional discounts on that order line.
  • The system automatically compares the single unstacked discount against the sum of competing stacked discounts and awards the customer the better of the two deals without double-dipping.

---

chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 05: Products Catalog & Inventory Control (/admin/catalog, /admin/inventory)

The Products & Inventory Control module governs the entire physical life of products—from SKU master definition and multi-level category classification to multi-location warehouse management, units of measure conversions, kits and hampers, two-step stock transfers, and continuous physical cycle counts.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The "Single Stock Number" Blind Spot: In basic systems, a product has one global stock number (e.g. "50 units on hand"). Management has no idea if those 50 units are in the Nairobi central depot, the Mombasa branch, or on a rider's delivery van, leading to false promises to customers.
  • Lost Goods in Transit: Moving stock between warehouses or out on delivery vans is where theft and shrinkage occur. Traditional spreadsheets write off stock immediately upon dispatch, losing all accountability while goods are on the road. QSell introduces an In-Transit Ledger where goods remain on the company's books until formally acknowledged and received at the destination.
  • Stock Counts That Force Business Closures: Businesses often shut down operations for an entire weekend to conduct physical inventory counts. In QSell, Continuous Cycle Counting allows warehouse staff to count shelves while retail cashiers and the web shop continue selling without discrepancy errors.
  • Unit of Measure Confusion: Selling a product in pieces, 12-packs, and 24-box cartons typically causes inventory chaos. QSell enforces strict base-unit decimal conversions (e.g., kilograms, litres, pieces).

Target Client Profiles

  • Multi-Branch Retailers & Wholesalers: Operating central distribution hubs, regional branch stores, and mobile van-sales fleets.
  • Hardware, Agro-Dealers & Building Suppliers: Selling goods by weight, length, volume, or pack sizes (cement, paint, fertilizer, cabling).
  • Gift, Hamper & Food Distributors: Assembling multi-item gift hampers and combo kits priced as a single unit but fulfilled and taxed as individual components.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you always know exactly what you have, exactly where it sits, and what it is worth. Your inventory isn't just a number on a spreadsheet—it is an immutable ledger. You can see real-time stock across every warehouse, branch shop, and delivery van. When you move stock between locations, it is tracked in transit. And best of all, you can perform physical stock audits on your shelves during business hours while your cashiers keep ringing up sales."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Zero Shrinkage in Transit: Two-step transfers require sender dispatch and receiver sign-off with variance reporting.
  • Zero Interrupted Trading: Continuous cycle counts eliminate the need for costly weekend store closures.
  • Kit Component Explosion: Bundles automatically deduct stock and calculate KRA tax for individual underlying components.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    UOM[1. Units of Measure: Pcs, Kg, Box Defined] --> CLAS[2. Business Classifications: Stocked, Service]
    CLAS --> LOC[3. Stock Locations Created: Warehouses, Stores, Vans]
    LOC --> CAT[4. Categories & Tax Classes Mapped]
    CAT --> PROD[5. SKUs & Kits Configured]
    PROD --> CUT[6. Stock Ledger Opening Balance Cutover]
  1. Units of Measure: Defined under /admin/settings/units (Base units and conversion multipliers).
  2. Business Classifications: Defined under /admin/item-types (Determining whether an item is physical stock, service, or consumable).
  3. Stock Locations: Defined under /admin/inventory/locations (At least one default warehouse or shop).
  4. Categories: Created under /admin/categories with mapped KRA tax classifications.
  5. Staff Permissions:
  • products:read, products:manage: Create and manage catalog SKUs.
  • stock:read, stock:manage: View stock levels, issue transfers, and conduct counts.
  • stock:cutover: Execute initial opening balance migration.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Products & Inventory module is divided into two operational domains:

graph TD
    subgraph CatalogDomain["Catalog Definition (/admin/catalog)"]
        PROD["Products Master & SKUs"]
        CAT["Category Hierarchy"]
        CLAS["Business Classifications"]
        UOM["Units of Measure & Decimals"]
        KITS["Kits & Hampers (Bundles)"]
    end

    subgraph InventoryDomain["Warehouse Management (/admin/inventory)"]
        LOC["Stock Locations (Depot, Shop, Van)"]
        BAL["Stock Balances: On-Hand vs Reserved"]
        TRANS["Stock Transfers & In-Transit"]
        COUNTS["Physical Cycle Counts & Audits"]
        LEDGER["Immutable Stock Ledger"]
    end

    CatalogDomain --> InventoryDomain

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Sub-Module 1: Products Master (/admin/products)

  • Product Directory: Server-paged table with instant filtering by Category, Stock Status (In Stock, Low Stock, Out of Stock), Classification, and Channel visibility.
  • Product Editor (/admin/products/[id]):
  • Basic Info: Title, SKU, Barcode (EAN-13/UPC), Brand, Category, Short Description, and HTML Rich-Text Body.
  • Pricing & Tax: Selling Price, Cost Price (for gross margin calculation), KRA Tax Classification (16% VAT, Zero-Rated, Exempt).
  • Stock & Units: Unit of Measure picker, Minimum Reorder Threshold, Safety Stock, and Track Inventory toggle.
  • Web Shop Flags: Show on Web Shop toggle, SEO title/description, and high-resolution gallery image uploader.

Sub-Module 2: Trash (/admin/trash/products)

  • Soft-delete recovery screen. Products removed from the catalog can be Restored as Drafts or permanently purged (only if no historic transaction or stock ledger records exist).

Sub-Module 3: Business Classifications (/admin/item-types)

  • Establishes product accounting behavior:
  • Stocked Goods: Physical inventory tracked in warehouses.
  • Non-Stocked Services: Labor, installation, delivery fees, consulting.
  • Consumables / Packaging: Boxes, tape, branded bags used at checkout.
  • Controls whether the item is "Sold to Customers" across quotes, orders, and storefront.

Sub-Module 4: Units of Measure (/admin/settings/units)

  • Global table of measurement units (e.g., PCS, KG, LTR, BOX, MTR).
  • Enforces decimal precision (e.g. Kilograms allow 3 decimals 1.425 kg, while Pieces allow 0 decimals 1 pc).
  • Defines conversion ratios (e.g., 1 Box = 24 Pieces).

Sub-Module 5: Categories (/admin/categories)

  • Multi-level tree view for organizing products into departments, categories, and subcategories. Drives storefront mega-menus and automated KRA tax inheritance.

Sub-Module 6: Kits and Hampers (/admin/pricing/kits)

  • Bundle creator: Defines combo packages (e.g., "Solar Home Kit 1kVA" or "Executive Christmas Hamper").
  • Line component mapping: Links 4 individual panels, 1 inverter, 2 batteries, and 1 mounting kit into a single sellable SKU.
  • Component Tax Handling: Automatically apportions VAT across components with differing tax rates.

Sub-Module 7: Stock Locations (/admin/inventory/locations)

  • Defines physical locations:
  • Warehouses: Central distribution godowns.
  • Retail Stores: Front-office shops where point-of-sale orders draw inventory.
  • Delivery Vans: Mobile stock locations assigned to riders for run dispatch.
  • Quarantine / Damaged: Holding locations for defective customer returns.

Sub-Module 8: Stock by Location (/admin/inventory/by-location)

  • Real-time stock matrix displaying product rows across location columns, showing:
  • On-Hand: Total physical units on shelves.
  • Reserved: Units committed to active customer orders awaiting dispatch.
  • Available: Uncommitted stock available to promise (On-Hand - Reserved).

Sub-Module 9: Stock Transfers (/admin/inventory/transfers)

  • Two-step inter-location workflow:
  1. Dispatch Transfer: Source location picks and dispatches goods. Stock moves from source On-Hand to In-Transit.
  2. Receive Transfer: Destination location inspects physical delivery and accepts goods. Stock moves from In-Transit to destination On-Hand.
  3. Discrepancy Reporting: Records damaged or missing items during transit.

Sub-Module 10: Stock Counts (/admin/inventory/counts)

  • Cycle counting engine:
  • Create a count session for a specific warehouse, aisle, or category.
  • Staff scan barcodes and record physical counts on mobile or desktop.
  • System freezes an inventory snapshot at count initiation: Cashiers keep selling!
  • Reconciliation view highlights positive/negative variances with KES financial impact.
  • Manager approves count, posting adjustment entries to the stock ledger.

Sub-Module 11: Stock Ledger & Cutover (/admin/inventory/ledger)

  • The single source of truth: An immutable, append-only log of every physical movement (receipts, sales dispatches, transfers, adjustments, returns, write-offs).
  • Includes the Cutover Wizard used during client onboarding to import verified opening inventory balances.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

Product SKU Master Fields (/admin/products/new)

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Product TitleName displayed on shop & quotes.Text (Max 160 chars)RequiredMust be unique within company.
SKU CodeUnique internal stock identifier.Text (Alphanumeric, Max 40)RequiredUppercase recommended (e.g. SLR-PAN-500W).
BarcodeEAN/UPC barcode for POS scanners.Text (Max 48 chars)OptionalMust be unique across all active products.
CategoryOrganizational department.DropdownRequiredDetermines tax rate and storefront navigation.
Unit of MeasureSelling unit.DropdownRequiredSelect from active UOMs (e.g. Piece, Box).
Selling PriceBase retail price.Currency (KES)RequiredInclusive or exclusive of VAT per company setting.
Cost PriceLanded purchase cost.Currency (KES)RequiredUsed for margin floors and gross profit KPI.
Tax ClassificationKRA eTIMS tax rate.DropdownRequiredGeneral Rate (16%), Zero-Rated (0%), Exempt.
Track InventoryEnables warehouse stock tracking.Toggle (On/Off)RequiredSet to Off for services and digital goods.
Low Stock ThresholdAlert trigger limit.Integer / DecimalOptionalGenerates dashboard attention warning when stock drops below.

Stock Transfer Fields (/admin/inventory/transfers/new)

Origin LocationSource warehouse or shop.DropdownRequiredMust have sufficient available stock.
Destination LocationReceiving warehouse or van.DropdownRequiredCannot equal Origin Location.
Product Line: SKUItem being transferred.Lookup AutocompleteRequiredMust exist at Origin Location.
Product Line: QtyNumber of units to move.Decimal / IntegerRequiredCannot exceed Origin's available stock.
Carrier / DriverPerson or courier moving goods.Text (Max 120 chars)OptionalStaff driver or courier tracking code.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Executing an Inter-Branch Stock Transfer

  1. Navigate to /admin/inventory/transfers and click New Transfer.
  2. Select Origin Location: "Central Depot - Industrial Area".
  3. Select Destination Location: "Westlands Retail Store".
  4. In the lines section, search for the product (e.g., "100Ah Deep Cycle Battery").
  5. Enter Quantity: 10. The system verifies that 10 units are available at Central Depot.
  6. Click Dispatch Transfer.
  7. An InlineConfirm prompt appears: "Dispatch 10 units into In-Transit status?" Click Confirm Dispatch.
  8. Print the Transfer Delivery Note for the driver.
  9. When the truck arrives at Westlands, the storekeeper opens /admin/inventory/transfers, selects the transfer, and clicks Receive Goods.
  10. If all 10 arrived safely, click Accept All into Stock.
  11. If 1 battery was cracked during transport, enter Received: 9, Damaged: 1.
  12. Click Confirm Receipt. The system places 9 batteries into Westlands stock and automatically routes the 1 damaged battery into the Quarantine location.

Action 2: Conducting a Cycle Count While Trading Continues

  1. Navigate to /admin/inventory/counts and click Start New Count.
  2. Select Location: "Mombasa Road Showroom".
  3. Select Scope: "Lighting & Fixtures" category.
  4. Click Initialize Count Session.
  5. The system captures an immutable snapshot of current book stock. Staff take barcode scanners to the shelves and scan physical items.
  6. Even if a customer buys a light bulb at the counter while the count is underway, the system's timestamped calculation accounts for the transaction without throwing off the audit.
  7. Click Review Variances.
  8. The screen displays discrepancies (e.g. Book Stock: 42, Physical Scanned: 40, Variance: -2 units, Financial Loss: KES 1,600).
  9. Enter an explanation reason: "Damaged showroom display units written off".
  10. Click Approve & Post Adjustments.
  11. Stock balances are instantly aligned with physical reality, and an inventory write-off entry is posted to the General Ledger.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

The Three Stock Numbers (On-Hand, Reserved, Available)

$$\text{Available Stock} = \text{On-Hand Stock} - \text{Active Unfulfilled Reservations}$$

  • On-Hand: Physical boxes on the shelf.
  • Reserved: Goods promised to orders currently being packed or awaiting dispatch.
  • Available: What the storefront and sales reps can sell. An order for 10 units will be refused if only 8 units are Available, even if 15 units are physically On-Hand.

Deactivating a Stock Location

  • A location cannot be deleted or deactivated if:
  1. It holds physical On-Hand stock $> 0$.
  2. It has open in-flight stock transfers.
  3. It has active orders with unfulfilled reservations.
  • The system blocks deactivation with the message: "Cannot deactivate location: 14 units remain on hand. Transfer or write off stock first."

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

StepVerification TaskExpected ResultPass/Fail
1Create Base Units of Measure (PCS with 0 decimals, KG with 3 decimals).Decimal constraints enforced accurately during entry.[ ]
2Create Central Warehouse, Retail Shop, and Van locations.Locations appear in Stock by Location matrix.[ ]
3Execute Opening Balance Cutover via Stock Ledger Wizard.On-hand quantities reflect physical counts accurately.[ ]
4Perform a 2-step stock transfer from Warehouse to Retail Shop.Stock moves to In-Transit upon dispatch, and to destination upon receipt.[ ]
5Build a Kit Product and place a test order.Master kit is sold; individual component stock quantities are deducted.[ ]

Guide 06: Delivery Logistics & Field Dispatch (/admin/delivery)

The Delivery & Field Logistics module orchestrates the physical journey of goods from the dispatch warehouse to the customer's doorstep. It governs polygon delivery zoning, dynamic rate calculation (by zone, weight, or distance), visual dispatch boards, rider run sequencing, Cash-on-Delivery (COD) custody reconciliation, third-party courier APIs, and scheduled on-site installation visits.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The "No Postcode" Reality in Africa: Standard international e-commerce software assumes structured postal codes (ZIP codes). In Kenya, addresses are descriptive (e.g., "Westlands, Muthithi Road, opposite Unga House, 3rd Floor"). QSell allows customers to either select localized zones (County $\rightarrow$ Town $\rightarrow$ Estate) or drop a GPS pin on the map, finding the exact delivery zone and fee automatically.
  • Cash on Delivery (COD) Reconciliation Black Holes: Riders collect cash and direct M-Pesa payments at customer doorsteps. In manual systems, days pass before riders hand in cash, leading to lost money, disputed balances, and theft. QSell treats Rider Cash Custody as a living ledger: every shilling collected is recorded against the rider's profile, and the cashier must formally accept the cash handover to clear the rider.
  • Unverified Third-Party Courier Billing: Couriers invoice merchants at the end of the month, and most businesses pay these invoices blindly. In QSell, what each courier charged for each parcel is recorded against that parcel as it happens. When the courier's invoice arrives, the office types it in and matches it to those recorded charges; the screen says plainly whether the two agree, or the invoice is higher or lower, and by how much. Charges the courier has made that no invoice has yet covered are listed so nothing is forgotten, and a charge can sit on one invoice only, so the same parcel cannot be paid twice.
  • Overpromising and Missed Delivery Windows: Dispatchers accept more orders than their vehicle fleet can carry. QSell enforces Delivery Slots with Capacity Limits (and a weight limit if wanted), closing a slot once it is full, and refusing times that are too soon for the goods to be ready. The shopper chooses a day and time at checkout; the promise is shown on the dispatch board and on the customer's tracking page.
  • Finding out a delivery is late only when the customer complains: Every delivery promised a time window is watched. It is flagged At risk before the window ends and Late after it, and a delivery that stays late goes up to the supervisor. The dispatchers and supervisors can be mailed automatically, and every flagged delivery is acknowledged with a note saying what is being done about it.
  • Riders who share one login, or whose phones are not secure: A rider with an account of their own signs in with their phone number and a 6-digit PIN, chosen by the rider and known only to them. Wrong guesses shut the rider out for a while, so a lost or borrowed phone is not a way in. A rider can see their own earnings and what they have been paid, which ends the daily argument about pay.
  • Not knowing whether delivery makes money: The delivery report and the performance screen show what customers paid for delivery against what it cost (rider pay, courier charges, fuel, vehicle costs), and how often deliveries are on time, succeed at the first try, and how full each delivery time runs.

Target Client Profiles

  • Omnichannel Retailers & E-Commerce Brands: Operating in-house motorcycle fleets or hybrid fleets (own riders for local delivery, couriers for upcountry).
  • FMCG & Beverage Distributors: Managing multi-drop truck and van delivery runs with cash settlement upon delivery.
  • Solar PV, Electronics & Equipment Suppliers: Requiring technical crews to visit customer premises, complete installation checklists, and capture digital customer sign-offs.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, delivery is no longer an operational headache that eats away your profit. Whether you use your own motorcycle riders, third-party couriers, or have customers collect at your counter, QSell handles it seamlessly. Your customers can drop a pin on a map or pick their estate; your dispatch board clusters orders into optimized delivery runs; riders confirm deliveries using the customer's delivery code; and any cash collected at the door is locked in a digital custody ledger until handed to your cashier."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% Cash-on-Delivery Accountability: Zero unrecorded door payments; riders cannot start new runs until previous cash floats are reconciled.
  • 15–20% Reduction in Last-Mile Delivery Spend: Automated distance/weight rate cards prevent undercharging customers for shipping.
  • Protection Against Courier Overbilling: Each courier invoice is checked against the charges recorded for that courier's parcels, and a charge cannot be counted on two invoices.
  • Fewer Late Deliveries Going Unnoticed: Every delivery promised a window is raised at risk, late and still-late, once each, with a record of who acknowledged it and what they said.
  • Fewer Rider Pay Disputes: Pay is recorded as each delivery is made, taken back only with a written reason, and paid out in one payout that is kept for good.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

    LOC[1. Stock Locations & Dispath Origins Set] --> ZONE[2. Delivery Zones & Polygons Defined]
