4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

1. Deliveries (/admin/delivery/deliveries)

  • Master directory of fulfillment parcels. Filter by Status (Draft, Released, Picking, Packed, Ready, On Run, Delivered, Failed), Method, and Branch. Supports Partial Dispatches (sending in-stock items while back-ordering the rest).

2. Delivery Zones (/admin/delivery/zones)

  • Geographic zone builder: Group counties, towns, and estates (e.g. "Nairobi Central", "Westlands & Parklands", "Thika & Environs"). Supports polygon geofencing on an interactive map.

3. Dispatch Board (/admin/delivery/dispatch)

  • Visual operations kanban:
  • Ready for Dispatch: Orders packed and waiting for transport.
  • Assigned to Run: Grouped by rider or vehicle.
  • Out for Delivery: Live monitoring of parcels currently on the road.
  • With couriers: Parcels handed to a courier, with its tracking number and last news.
  • A delivery promised a time shows a chip such as Promised Fri 6 Nov, 09:00 to 12:00, turning At risk and then Late using the company's own warning time (see Late Deliveries).
  • A parcel whose booking with the courier's system failed (or whose cancellation failed) shows a Courier not booked chip.

4. Delivery Runs (/admin/delivery/runs)

  • Multi-drop trip management: Sequenced list of stops for a rider. Calculates total run weight, departure time, estimated arrival at each stop, and starting cash float.

5. Riders (/admin/delivery/riders)

  • Who rides: choose whether the company uses its own staff as riders, riders with an account of their own, or both. A kind cannot be switched off while people of that kind are still working.
  • Proof at the door: what a rider must show to mark a delivery delivered (nothing, the customer's code, a photo, or either).
  • Add a member of staff as a rider (the staff member keeps signing in with their own account) or Make an account for a rider (an account that opens the rider app and nothing else).
  • Each rider's card: kind, email, phone, vehicle, branch, runs still to do, and status (Riding, Paused, Left); buttons to pause, resume, mark as left, and (for riders with their own account) give a new first password.
  • Sign in with a phone number and PIN (riders with their own account only): the rider's PIN panel shows No PIN, Waiting for the rider to choose their own, PIN set or Shut out for ..., the number they sign in with, when they last signed in, and any wrong tries in a row. Buttons: Give a PIN, Give a new PIN, Let them try again, Turn off the PIN. See Action 4.

6. Door Payments (/admin/delivery/door-payments)

  • Cash custody ledger: Shows cash and M-Pesa collected by each rider at customer doors.
  • Reconciles rider cash against the counter till during evening debrief.

7. Delivery Costs (/admin/delivery/costs)

  • What riders are paid: what a rider earns for each delivery made and for each day on a run on which something was delivered (once a day, however many runs). Either can be nothing. Pay already earned never changes when the rules change.
  • Fuel and vehicle costs: type in fuel, a vehicle cost (repairs, service, parking, tolls) or another cost, with what it was for, and optionally the run it belongs to. See Action 8.
  • Costs: every cost, newest first, filtered by kind and by days. Rider pay is recorded as deliveries are made; a courier's charge is typed on the delivery it belongs to. A mistake is never edited: it is taken back with a written reason, and the original stays on record.
  • In the books: the two accounts rider pay is posted to. Pay is saved first and posted afterwards, so a mistake in the accounts never stops a rider's delivery; what is waiting is counted and can be posted at once.
  • Owed to riders / Paid to riders: what each rider is owed (pay earned less anything taken back, not yet paid) and the payouts made, each with its number.

8. Late Deliveries (/admin/delivery/late)

  • Every delivery promised a window that is At risk or Late now, the most overdue first, showing how late, the highest level reached (At risk: the dispatcher is told, Late: the dispatcher is told, Still late: the supervisor is told), when it was raised, and how many mails were sent about it (sent, waiting, could not be sent).
  • Each has an Acknowledge box (What is being done about it) that records who answered, when and what they said. One acknowledgement covers every level raised for that window.

9. Delivery Slots (/admin/delivery/slots)

  • Slots: the delivery times a branch offers (for example Morning 09:00 to 12:00), the days of the week they run, how many deliveries a day each can take, how many minutes before the start an order must be placed, and optionally the most weight it can carry in a day. A slot can be stopped (deliveries already promised it keep it).
  • Days with no slots: close a day for all branches or one (public holidays, stock-taking), with the reason.
  • How long the goods need (lead times): the least time from order to ready, for a delivery zone or for an item (for example fresh or made-to-order goods). A delivery cannot be promised a slot that starts before the longest lead time that applies.
  • When a delivery counts as late: how many minutes before the end of the window a delivery is At risk, after how many minutes late it goes to the supervisor, and who is mailed at each level.
  • At checkout the shopper sees the days and times that are open; one that fills before the order is made is never a reason to refuse the sale. See Conditions and Rules.

10. Couriers (/admin/delivery/couriers)

  • The courier companies the business sends parcels with. A courier is either by hand (the office types its tracking number and news) or connected to its own system over the internet: the system then books each parcel, follows it, and cancels it with the courier by itself. A courier's own system is connected through settings (its web address, the header that carries your key, the paths used to book, ask about and cancel a parcel, and where its answers keep the tracking number and status); no programming is needed for couriers whose system speaks the common web format, and a specific courier's own connection can be added later.
  • The key the courier gave you is kept sealed and never shown again. The secret that signs the courier's news (so that only the real courier can report to you) is shown once, together with the address the courier is to send its news to.
  • A courier can be stopped and started, edited (two people editing at once are warned), and given a new secret.

11. Visits (/admin/delivery/visits)

  • Technical installation crew scheduling: Assigns technicians to site visits (e.g. solar PV installation, air-conditioner servicing). Provides digital checklists and captures customer signatures on site.

12. Delivery Report (/admin/delivery/reports)

  • Executive analytics: Delivery success rates, failure reason distributions (e.g. customer unavailable, wrong address), and zone profitability.

13. Courier Invoices (/admin/delivery/courier-invoices)

  • Charged to us, on no invoice yet: by courier, how many charges and how much have not been put on any invoice.
  • Type in an invoice: the courier, the invoice number, the day on the invoice, the invoice total and an optional note. The invoice is typed in; it is not read from an uploaded file.
  • Each invoice shows its total, the charges matched to it and the difference, with a status: Nothing matched yet, Agrees with our charges, We have fewer charges than the invoice, or We have more charges than the invoice. Match charges lists that courier's charges that are on no invoice, to tick; matched charges can be taken off. A wrong invoice is voided with a reason.
  • Matching changes no charge and posts nothing; paying the invoice is done in the usual way.

14. Delivery Performance (/admin/delivery/performance)

  • For the days chosen (the last 30 by default, at most a year): Overall (deliveries made, % on time, % at the first try, average time from going out to delivered, how late the late ones were, release-to-delivered time), By rider, By courier (parcels sent and what became of them, including parcels that could not be booked), and Delivery times (places offered, booked, days full and share used for each slot; how many times shoppers chose at checkout and how many had gone by delivery).
  • On time means delivered by the end of the window the customer was promised; deliveries promised no window are left out of that rate. First try means no failed attempt before. Rates are marked good (95% and over), to watch (80% and over) or poor.

15. Delivery Charges (/admin/delivery/charges)

  • Rate card matrix: Configure pricing rules:
  • Flat Rate per Zone (e.g. Nairobi CBD: KES 250).
  • Weight-Tier Matrix (e.g. 0-5 kg: KES 300, KES 50 per additional kg).
  • Distance Formula (e.g. Base KES 200 + KES 35/km from branch pin).
  • Free Shipping Thresholds (e.g. Free delivery for orders over KES 10,000).

16. Delivery Methods (/admin/delivery/methods)

  • Per-branch toggle enabling or disabling specific fulfillment modes (Own Fleet, Courier, In-Store Collection, Installation Visit).

17. Delivery Invoicing (/admin/delivery/invoicing)

  • KRA Tax compliance setting: Choose whether delivery charges appear on the Same Tax Invoice as products, or on a Separate Delivery Invoice signed independently for KRA eTIMS.

18. Stock Timing (/admin/delivery/stock)

  • Configures the exact moment stock is deducted from the physical ledger:
  • Option A: When order is paid.
  • Option B: When packed into dispatch vehicle.
  • Option C: When customer confirms receipt at the door.

19. Map Service (/admin/delivery/maps)

  • Provider configuration: Toggle between free OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) or Google Maps Platform for address autocomplete and distance calculations, comparing cost vs. accuracy tradeoffs.

20. The Rider App (/rider)

  • Sign in (/rider/sign-in): a rider with an account of their own enters their Phone number and PIN. A link underneath offers Sign in with email and password instead (used by staff who ride, and still available to any rider).
  • Choose your own PIN (/rider/pin): shown the first time after the office gives a PIN, and later from Change my PIN. Until the rider has chosen their own PIN, every other page of the app brings them back here.
  • My runs (/rider): runs still to do and the last few finished; a notice of the cash the rider holds from doors; a link to My pay; the runs kept on the phone open without signal.
  • A run and its stops: each stop with the customer's name, address, phone, items and links to call, chat and navigate; buttons to mark delivered or failed; cash and M-Pesa collected at the door; finishing the run.
  • My pay (/rider/pay): Owed to me now (earned and not yet paid), Earned this month, What I earned (the latest 30 entries, each marked Paid or Not paid yet; pay the office took back shows as Taken back by the office, without the office's reason) and What was paid to me (the latest 10 payouts with number, day, how it was paid and reference). A rider sees only their own.
  • Sign out at the top, back to the rider sign-in.

21. What the Customer Sees

  • At checkout: for a delivery, the days and times that are open (with places left), and the earliest time; the shopper's choice is kept with the order. If the chosen time has filled by the time the delivery is made, the sale and the delivery go ahead and the customer is sent a message saying the time could not be kept; the office sees what the customer chose and what became of it on the order.
  • On the tracking page: the promised window until it is delivered, and, for a parcel with a courier that gave a page, a link Follow it on their page.

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Planning and Dispatching a Multi-Drop Delivery Run

  1. Navigate to /admin/delivery/dispatch.
  2. The board lists orders in Ready for Dispatch status.
  3. Click Create Delivery Run.
  4. Select Fulfilling Branch: "Nairobi Industrial Area".
  5. Select Assigned Rider: "David Mutua (Motorcycle #KMDF 123A)".
  6. In the orders list, select the 4 customer orders destined for Westlands.
  7. Click Add to Run.
  8. In the Stop Order list, drag and drop the stops into optimal street delivery sequence.
  9. Click Finalize & Dispatch Run.
  10. The system prompts: "Confirm dispatch of 4 parcels? Stock will move to David Mutua's mobile custody."
  11. Click Confirm Dispatch.
  12. The run status updates to Out for Delivery, and the parcels appear immediately on David Mutua's mobile phone at /rider.

Action 2: Customer Handover & Verification PIN Confirmation

  1. The rider arrives at the customer's address and opens the /rider mobile web app.
  2. Selects the active stop: "Order #ORD-10492 - Jane Wanjiku".
  3. The rider asks for the 6-digit delivery code the customer was sent in the "on its way" message (by email) when the delivery left. The customer gives it only when the parcel arrives. (If the company's rule at the door is a photo, or nothing, the app asks for that instead; see Proof at the door on the Riders screen.)
  4. The rider types the code (for example 048213) into the app.
  5. If the order is Cash on Delivery, the rider selects Payment Collected:
  • Types cash amount received: KES 3,500.00.
  1. Click Confirm Delivery.
  2. The system validates the code instantly, marks the delivery as Delivered, updates the customer order status, and adds KES 3,500.00 to David Mutua's cash custody ledger.

Action 3: Reconciling Evening Cash Handover from a Rider

  1. At the end of the shift, the rider returns to the cashier desk.
  2. The cashier navigates to /admin/delivery/door-payments.
  3. In the rider list, select David Mutua.
  4. The screen displays: "Total Cash Custody: KES 14,200.00 (from 4 deliveries today)".
  5. The rider hands the physical cash to the cashier.
  6. The cashier counts KES 14,200.00, selects the destination till ("Main Cash Till #1"), and clicks Accept Cash Handover.
  7. An InlineConfirm prompt appears: "Accept KES 14,200.00 from David Mutua into Main Cash Till #1?"
  8. Click Confirm Handover.
  9. The rider's custody balance drops to zero, and a cash receipt journal entry is posted to the till ledger.

Action 4: Giving a Rider a PIN, and the Rider's First Sign-In

  1. Open /admin/delivery/riders. The rider must have an account of their own, a Kenyan mobile number and be riding or paused.
  2. On the rider's card, in Sign in with a phone number and PIN, click Give a PIN.
  3. A yellow box shows six digits, for example 482915, with the number the rider signs in with. This is the only time the PIN is shown; the system does not keep it. Give it to the rider in person or by a call. Click I have given it to them.
  4. The rider opens /rider; being signed out, they are taken to the sign-in. They enter their phone number and the PIN and click Sign in.
  5. They are taken to Choose your own PIN. They enter the PIN the office gave, then a new PIN twice. Weak PINs are refused with the reason shown under the box. Click Save my PIN.
  6. They arrive at My runs. The rider's card now shows PIN set and when they last signed in.
  7. To give a new PIN (a forgotten PIN), click Give a new PIN and confirm. The old PIN stops working and any phone signed in with it is signed out within a minute; the rider repeats steps 4 to 6.
  8. To stop the PIN, click Turn off the PIN and confirm. The rider can then sign in only with email and password.

Action 5: When a Rider Is Shut Out

  1. After five wrong tries in a row the rider sees Too many wrong tries. Try again in 15 minutes. Further wrong tries lengthen the wait (30 minutes, 1 hour, up to 4 hours). Even the right PIN does not work until the wait is over.
  2. The rider's card shows Shut out for .... Click Let them try again to clear it at once, or leave it to run out.
  3. A wrong number and a wrong PIN get the same answer, so someone guessing cannot learn which numbers belong to riders.

Action 6: Handling a Late Delivery

  1. Open /admin/delivery/late (or watch the mail the dispatchers receive, if mail addresses are set).
  2. Find the delivery: its card shows how late it is and the highest level reached.
  3. Act on it (call the rider, tell the customer, move the delivery to another run).
  4. In What is being done about it type what you did (a few words) and click Acknowledge. The answer, your name and the time are kept; the card then shows who acknowledged it.
  5. The delivery leaves the screen once it is delivered, cancelled or returned.

Action 7: Connecting a Courier and Sending a Parcel

  1. Open /admin/delivery/couriers and fill Add a courier: the Name, How it is connected, and, for a connected courier, the web address, the key and the paths from the courier's documents. Click Add the courier.
  2. For a connected courier, a box shows the address the courier sends its news to and the secret that signs its news. Copy both now and give them to the courier; the secret is not shown again. Click I have copied it.
  3. On a ready delivery that goes by courier, choose the courier under Courier from your list (or type a name for a courier by hand and a tracking number) and dispatch it. Dispatch happens at once.
  4. The system books the parcel with the courier within a minute. If the courier cannot be reached it tries again after 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 minutes, then shows the failure on the delivery and the board; Try the courier again tries at once. A courier being down never holds up a dispatch.
  5. The system asks the courier about the parcel while it is on the road (every 15 minutes at first, then less often); Ask the courier now does it at once. News the courier sends to the address is accepted only if correctly signed.
  6. When the courier reports delivered, the delivery is completed with who signed and a link to the proof. A problem reported by the courier becomes a failed attempt. A cancelled delivery is cancelled with the courier by the system.
  7. To stop using a courier, click Stop using and confirm; Make a new secret replaces the signing secret (the old one stops working).

Action 8: Recording Fuel and Other Running Costs

  1. Open /admin/delivery/costs. In Fuel and vehicle costs choose What kind of cost, type How much (KSh) and What it was for, and optionally pick the Run it was for.
  2. Click Save the cost. A confirmation appears and the form empties; clicking twice saves it once.
  3. The cost appears in the list and counts in the delivery report. It is not posted to the accounts here: record the receipt as an expense or a supplier invoice in the usual way, so it is not counted twice.
  4. If it was typed wrongly, type Why it is being taken back on its row and confirm Take it back.

Action 9: Typing In and Matching a Courier Invoice

  1. Open /admin/delivery/courier-invoices. Under Type in an invoice choose the courier, type the number, the day and the total, and click Record the invoice.
  2. The invoice appears as Nothing matched yet. Click Match charges to ....
  3. Tick the courier's charges that appear on the invoice and click the Match button (it shows how many and how much).
  4. The invoice shows what was matched and the difference: Agrees with our charges, or fewer or more charges than the invoice. Decide what to do about a difference (ask the courier, or find the missing charge).
  5. To correct a mistake, click Take off beside a charge and confirm, or void the whole invoice by typing Why it is being voided and confirming Void it.

Action 10: Paying a Rider

  1. Open /admin/delivery/costs, Owed to riders.
  2. Find the rider and click Pay. Choose Paid by and, if you have one, type the Reference, then click the pay button (it shows the amount).
  3. The payout is numbered, the rider's balance clears, and (when the books are live and the accounts are chosen) the accounts are posted. The rider sees it under What was paid to me.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

Handling a Failed Delivery Attempt

  • If a rider arrives and the customer is unreachable:
  1. The rider clicks Report Failed Attempt in the mobile app.
  2. The system forces selection of a mandatory Failure Reason Code:
  • Customer Phone Unreachable
  • Customer Not at Premises
  • Customer Refused / Cash Shortage
  • Inaccessible Road / Weather Block
  1. The rider must enter a short memo note.
  2. The delivery transitions to Attempt Failed. Stock remains in the rider's custody until the run is closed, where it must be physically returned to the warehouse storekeeper.

Invoicing Modes for Delivery Charges (KRA Compliance)

Under /admin/delivery/invoicing, the business configures one of two fiscal modes:

  • Combined Invoicing: Delivery is printed as a service line item on the primary product tax invoice, taxed at the standard 16% VAT rate.
  • Separate Delivery Invoicing: Products are billed on Invoice A, while the delivery fee is billed on a separate Delivery Invoice B. This is required when delivery is handled by an affiliated logistics entity with a separate KRA PIN.

Rider PIN Sign-In: Rules

  • Only riders with an account of their own sign in with a PIN. A member of staff who rides always signs in with their own account: a PIN must never open a back-office account.
  • A PIN sign-in opens the rider app only, whatever the account holds.
  • The system never keeps a PIN, only a scrambled form made with a secret of the server's own. The office sees a PIN once, when it is given.
  • A rider who is paused, has left, whose account is switched off, or whose kind of rider has been switched off cannot sign in, even with the right PIN.
  • Changing a rider's phone number turns their PIN off (a PIN belongs to the number it was given for); a rider who leaves loses it, freeing the number for someone else. A phone number belongs to one rider at a time.
  • Sign-in attempts are also limited by device address and by phone number, so many guesses from many places run out as quickly as many from one. Someone repeatedly trying a rider's number can shut that rider out for a while; the office's Let them try again is the remedy.
  • A phone signed in with an old PIN is signed out when the PIN is changed, replaced or turned off (within about a minute).

Delivery Slots, Cut-Offs and Customer Choice

  • A shopper is offered a day and time only if the slot runs that day, the day is not closed, places are left, the weight limit is not passed, the cut-off has not passed and the goods can be ready in time (the longest lead time that applies).
  • The shopper's cut-off is judged at the moment they chose; a day that has already passed is refused.
  • The delivery is booked the slot when the delivery is made. If the slot has filled since, neither the sale nor the delivery is held up: the customer's request is marked as not kept, and the customer is sent a message in the same step.
  • A booked window is kept as promised, even if the slot is later changed or stopped.

Lateness

  • A delivery promised a window is On track, At risk (within the warning time of the end of the window, or the window has begun and it is not on its way), Late (past the end), On time or Delivered late. Cancelled and returned deliveries are not watched.
  • At risk, Late and Still late: the supervisor is told are each raised once for a delivery and a window; a delivery given a new window is watched afresh. A background task checks every minute.
  • Mail is queued in the same step that raises a level, one mail for each address; if the mail server is down the mail is tried again after 5, 10, 20 and 40 minutes and then left as could not be sent. A mail never carries an address, phone number or payment detail. Changing the list later does not change who was already told.

Couriers

  • Calls to a courier go only to secure (https) public addresses; the courier's own error text is never shown to staff, only a plain reason.
  • A booking that fails because the courier refused the request fails at once; one that fails because the courier could not be reached is retried. The same piece of news from a courier (pushed or asked) counts once.
  • Cancelling a delivery cancels its parcel with the courier; a parcel never booked is simply closed.

Costs, Pay and Courier Invoices

  • Costs are never edited or deleted; a mistake is taken back by an opposite entry with a reason, once. A cost taken back cannot be matched to a courier invoice.
  • Rider pay for a delivery is counted once however many times the delivery is retried. Pay for a day is counted once for a rider and a day.
  • What is owed to a rider is the pay earned less anything taken back, not yet paid out. If more was taken back than earned, nothing can be paid and the balance is set against their next pay.
  • Fuel and vehicle costs reduce the delivery margin in the report but are not posted to the accounts.
  • A courier charge is on at most one invoice; matching a set of charges is all or nothing; a voided invoice frees its charges and its number; an invoice's words cannot be changed once typed.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

StepVerification TaskExpected ResultPass/Fail
1Configure 3 Delivery Zones with towns and estates.Zones appear in storefront checkout dropdown.[ ]
2Configure a Distance-based Rate Card (KES 200 base + KES 30/km).Checkout pin-drop calculates exact distance and fee accurately.[ ]
3Make an account for a rider with a Kenyan mobile number, then Give a PIN.The PIN is shown once; the rider signs in at /rider with the number and PIN and is made to choose their own PIN before anything else.[ ]
4Plan a Delivery Run and dispatch 2 test orders.Parcels appear on rider run sheet; stock moves to mobile custody.[ ]
5Execute Door Payment collection and Cashier Handover.Rider custody ledger updates and clears to zero upon cashier sign-off.[ ]
6Try five wrong PINs for the test rider.The rider is shut out (even for the right PIN) and the card shows Shut out for ...; Let them try again restores sign-in.[ ]
7Give the test rider a new PIN while a phone is signed in with the old one.The old PIN fails and the old phone is signed out within a minute.[ ]
8Set rider pay (for example KES 50 for each delivery) and complete a test delivery.The rider's My pay shows the entry as Not paid yet; after Pay, it shows Paid and the payout.[ ]
9Record a fuel cost against a run.It appears in the cost list and in the delivery report's cost line, and is taken back with a reason on request.[ ]
10Add a slot with room for one delivery a day and book two orders.The second shopper is not offered the slot; a shopper whose chosen slot filled still completes the order and is sent a message.[ ]
11Give a delivery a window that has already ended, with mail addresses set.Within a minute the delivery appears on Late deliveries, the dispatchers are mailed, and acknowledging it records your note.[ ]
12Add a courier by hand and a connected courier (test key).The connected courier's news secret is shown once; the board shows Courier not booked if the test address cannot be reached, and Try the courier again retries.[ ]
13Type a courier invoice and match two charges.The invoice shows Agrees with our charges when the total equals the charges, or the difference when it does not; a charge cannot be matched twice.[ ]
14Open Delivery performance after a few test deliveries.On-time, first-try, rider, courier and delivery-time figures appear, and show nothing (not zero percent) where no delivery was promised a window.[ ]

Common Client Setup Pitfalls

  • A rider has a landline or foreign number: a PIN cannot be given. Correct the phone number on the rider first; changing it turns an existing PIN off.
  • Two riders share one phone number: the second cannot be given a PIN. Each rider needs their own number.
  • Slots exist but shoppers are never offered a time: the branch has no slot on that day of the week, the day is closed, the cut-off has passed, or a lead time makes the goods too late.
  • Lateness mail never arrives: no addresses were typed in the lateness settings, or the company's mail sending is not configured; the Late deliveries screen still shows everything.
  • Rider pay is recorded but not in the accounts: the books are not live, or the two accounts under In the books were not chosen. What is waiting is counted on the screen.
  • A courier invoice does not agree: a charge was never typed on the delivery, was taken back, or is already on another invoice. The difference shows how much is missing or extra.

chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 07: Users, Roles & Access Governance (/admin/users)

The Users & Access Governance module provides enterprise-grade identity, authentication, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC). It ensures that every staff member has precisely the permissions required for their operational responsibilities while enforcing strict separation of duties across cash handling, inventory management, procurement, and financial reporting.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The "Admin Password Shared by Everyone" Disaster: In many businesses, staff share a single master administrator login. When money goes missing, orders are deleted, or prices are discounted, management cannot hold any individual accountable. QSell mandates individual staff accounts with immutable audit logging for every action.
  • Internal Fraud & Collusion: If the person receiving goods in the warehouse can also create purchase orders and approve supplier invoices, fake deliveries and embezzlement inevitably follow. QSell enforces strict Separation of Duties (SoD) through granular atomic permissions.
  • Data Leakage Between Competing Branches: In multi-branch retail, store managers often compete for performance bonuses. Giving all staff global access causes friction and leakage of customer contact lists. QSell's Branch-Scoped Access restricts staff visibility strictly to their assigned operating location.
  • After-Hours System Tampering: Dishonest staff may log into the system late at night or from home to manipulate records. QSell's Access Policies (ABAC) allow management to enforce contextual constraints (e.g. "Logins only permitted Monday-Saturday between 7:00 AM and 7:00 PM from authorized company network IPs").

Target Client Profiles

  • Medium to Large Enterprises & Retail Chains: Employing 10 to 500+ staff across sales, logistics, warehousing, accounting, and executive leadership.
  • Franchise & Multi-Branch Operators: Requiring independent branch staff permissions with centralized corporate oversight.
  • Audit-Sensitive Corporations: Requiring proof of strict internal controls for external financial auditors and board compliance.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you have total control over who sees what and who can do what in your business. You can give a counter cashier the exact ability to ring up sales and print receipts, without letting them see your product cost prices or company profit. Your storekeepers can manage stock movements without touching invoices. And you can ensure that cashiers can only log into their till during business hours while physically at the store."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% Personal Accountability: Every single transaction, stage movement, and document edit is stamped with the authenticated user's ID.
  • Zero Margin Leakage to Frontline Staff: report_profit:read permission separates top-line sales figures from sensitive product cost prices.
  • Contextual Perimeter Defense: Time-of-day and IP-based access policies block unauthorized remote logins.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    BRAN[1. Operating Branches Configured] --> ROLES[2. Standard Roles Configured & Permissions Bound]
    ROLES --> POL[3. Optional ABAC Contextual Policies Created]
    POL --> USERS[4. User Accounts Created & Bound to Roles/Branches]
  1. Operating Branches: Defined under Settings > Branches so users can be assigned to physical operating units.
  2. Roles Defined: Built under /admin/users/roles with explicit permission bindings.
  3. Staff Account Creation: Users invited or created under /admin/users.
  4. Required Permissions: Only staff with users:read and users:manage can access this module.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

Access control is built upon a 3-layer security model:

graph TD
    USER["User Account (Email, Password, Assigned Branch)"]
    ROLE["Roles (e.g. Cashier, Storekeeper, Accountant)"]
    PERM["Atomic Permissions (e.g. orders:read, stock:manage)"]
    ABAC["Access Policies (Context: Time, IP, Device, Amount)"]

    USER --> ROLE
    ROLE --> PERM
    USER --> ABAC
    PERM --> ACCESS{"Grant or Deny Action?"}
    ABAC --> ACCESS
  1. Layer 1: Identity & Branch Scope: The authenticated user identity bound to a primary operating branch (or "All Branches" for corporate directors).
  2. Layer 2: Role-Based Permissions (RBAC): Role templates grouping atomic permissions across 10 system categories.
  3. Layer 3: Contextual Policies (ABAC): Dynamic rules that evaluate environmental attributes (time of day, network IP, document amount) before permitting an action.

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Sub-Module 1: Users Directory (/admin/users)

  • Master list of staff accounts showing Name, Email, Assigned Branch, Role(s), MFA Status, and Account State (Active, Suspended).
  • Actions: Invite User, Edit Account, Reset Password, Impersonate (Super Admin only), and Deactivate User.

Sub-Module 2: Roles & Permissions (/admin/users/roles)

  • Role catalog view showing pre-packaged and custom roles (e.g. Super Administrator, Branch Manager, Senior Accountant, Sales Representative, Storekeeper, Counter Cashier, Dispatcher).
  • Role Permission Matrix: Interactive accordion grouped into the 10 core permission categories:
  1. General (Dashboard, Analytics export).
  2. Orders & Sales (Read, create, edit, cancel orders, quotes, customers).
  3. Projects (Job costing, milestone approval).
  4. Vendor Management (RFQs, POs, RGN receipts, supplier invoices).
  5. Customers (Credit limit overrides, pricing group assignments).
  6. Products & Inventory (Catalog edits, stock transfers, cycle counts, ledger cutover).
  7. Finance & Payments (General journals, bank accounts, receipts, fiscal period closing).
  8. Reports & Insights (Sales, collections, gross profit, receivables ageing).
  9. Company & Settings (Brand profile, document layouts, payment gateways, KRA eTIMS).
  10. Users & Access (User creation, role configuration, access policies).

Sub-Module 3: Access Policies (/admin/users/policies)

  • Contextual policy designer:
  • Create rules combining attributes: If User Role = Cashier AND Current Time NOT BETWEEN 08:00 AND 18:00 THEN DENY LOGIN.
  • IP Whitelisting: If Action = Post General Journal AND User IP NOT IN [Head_Office_IPs] THEN REQUIRE MFA.

---

5. Standard Role Templates (Implementor Reference)

Role TemplatePrimary Target PersonaKey Granted PermissionsKey Restricted / Denied Permissions

Warehouse StorekeeperGodown and inventory staff.stock:read, stock:manage, inventory:counts, inventory:transfers, rgn:read, rgn:receiveDenied: orders:delete, gl_journals:post, company:write, supplier_invoices:read
Sales RepresentativeField and counter sales reps.quotes:manage, orders:create, customers:read, pricing:readDenied: pricing:override_unlimited, gl_journals:post, report_profit:read
Logistics DispatcherFleet coordinator.deliveries:read, deliveries:dispatch, riders:manage, delivery_runs:manageDenied: receipts:delete, finance:manage, gl_accounts:write
Senior AccountantBack-office finance team.finance:manage, gl_journals:post, bank_accounts:read, receipts:read, supplier_invoices:postDenied: users:manage, system:configure, stock:physical_count
Branch ManagerOperational head of a store.Scoped to assigned branch: all sales, stock, delivery, and branch report permissions.Denied: reports:all_branches, company:profile_write, tax_compliance:manage
Super AdministratorCompany directors and IT head.Full global access across all 10 categories, all branches, and all settings.None.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Onboarding a New Cashier Account

  1. Navigate to /admin/users and click New User.
  2. Enter Full Name: "Faith Mwangi".
  3. Enter Corporate Email: "faith.mwangi@company.co.ke".
  4. In the Primary Branch dropdown, select "Nairobi Westlands Store".
  5. In the Role selection list, check the box for Counter Cashier.
  6. Check the box Require Password Reset on First Login.
  7. Click Create User.
  8. The system dispatches an activation email to Faith Mwangi containing a secure, single-use login link.

Action 2: Creating a Custom Restricted Role for Sales Interns

  1. Navigate to /admin/users/roles and click New Role.
  2. Enter Role Name: "Sales Intern".
  3. Enter Description: "Can create draft quotes and view customers; cannot view costs or confirm orders."
  4. In the permissions list:
  • Expand Orders & Sales: Check quotes:read, quotes:create, customers:read.
  • Leave orders:confirm and orders:cancel unchecked.
  • Expand Reports & Insights: Leave report_profit:read unchecked.
  1. Click Save Role.
  2. A success message confirms: "Role 'Sales Intern' created with 3 active permissions."

Action 3: Enforcing Operating Hours via an Access Policy

  1. Navigate to /admin/users/policies and click New Access Policy.
  2. Enter Policy Name: "Cashier Operating Window".
  3. In the Target Roles picker, select Counter Cashier.
  4. In the Conditions builder:
  • Select Attribute: Current Time (Local).
  • Select Operator: Outside Hours.
  • Enter Time Range: 07:30 to 19:30.
  1. In the Action selector, choose Deny Access with Notice.
  2. Enter Customer Message: "System access is restricted outside operational retail hours. Please contact your Branch Manager."
  3. Click Activate Policy.
  4. Any cashier attempting to log in at 10:00 PM is immediately blocked with the configured message.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

Preventing Accidental Lockout (Super Admin Safeguard)

  • The system prevents deactivating or deleting the last active user holding the Super Administrator role.
  • If an administrator attempts to remove the users:manage permission from their own account, the system rejects the operation: "Cannot remove administrative access from your own active session."

Multi-Branch Visibility Isolation

  • Users with the reports:all_branches permission can view company-wide consolidated analytics.
  • Users lacking this permission have their queries automatically filtered at the database level by branch_id = user.assigned_branch_id.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

Guide 08: Projects & Job Costing (/admin/projects)

The Projects & Job Costing module manages complex, milestone-based customer deliverables, technical installations, and internal business initiatives. It tracks tasks, billable materials, direct labor expenses, customer milestone billings, and actual gross profitability per job.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The "Profitable on Paper, Loss in Reality" Trap: Service contractors and equipment installers (e.g. Solar PV installers, HVAC technicians, machinery distributors) often win projects with a high contract value, only to discover at completion that unexpected labor hours, extra cabling, and sub-contractor fees wiped out all profit. QSell tracks Budget vs. Actual Costs in real time as materials are dispatched and hours are logged.
  • Delayed Milestone Billing: In multi-stage projects (e.g. 30% Advance Deposit, 50% Delivery of Equipment, 20% Final Commissioning), businesses frequently forget to issue milestone invoices promptly, choking cash flow. QSell binds project tasks directly to Accounts Receivable billing schedules.
  • Premature Project Closure: Jobs are often marked "finished" while open vendor invoices or unreturned equipment remain unaccounted for. QSell enforces a strict state machine (draft $\rightarrow$ open $\rightarrow$ on_hold $\rightarrow$ completed $\rightarrow$ closed), preventing a project from being formally closed until all costs and billings reconcile.

Target Client Profiles

  • Solar PV & Renewable Energy Contractors: Managing residential and commercial solar installations requiring site assessments, panel mounts, inverters, wiring, and commissioning.
  • Commercial Equipment & Fit-Out Contractors: Installing industrial kitchen equipment, backup diesel generators, security CCTV systems, and retail shop fittings.
  • Internal Corporate Project Teams: Managing internal capital expenditure projects (e.g. opening a new retail branch or refurbishing a warehouse).

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you can quote, execute, and bill complex installation jobs with total financial clarity. You can build a project budget with materials from your warehouse and estimated labor costs, track every milestone task, issue customer milestone invoices, and watch your true gross margin update with every screw and hour spent. You will never finish a project wondering where your profit went."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Real-Time Job Profitability: Realized gross margin monitored continuously against initial quotation budgets.
  • Strict State-Machine Integrity: Projects cannot be prematurely closed with unbilled milestones or open tasks.
  • Zero Double-Keying: Direct quote-to-project-to-invoice workflows eliminate re-typing.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    CUST[1. Customer Account Created] --> CURR[2. Currency & Price Lists Defined]
    CURR --> PROD[3. Inventory SKUs & Labor Services Cataloged]
    PROD --> USR[4. Project Manager Assigned Permission: projects:read/manage]
    USR --> PROJ[5. Project Created & Opened]
  1. Customer Master Card: A customer must be selected under /admin/customers (unless the project is an internal company project).
  2. Catalog SKUs: Physical items (e.g. solar panels, inverters) and labor services (e.g. technical installation per day) must exist in the catalog.
  3. Staff Permissions: projects:read to view and projects:manage to create, edit, change status, and add tasks.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Project Lifecycle is governed by a deterministic, non-reversible state machine:

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft: Create Project
    draft --> open: Open Project (Approve Budget)
    draft --> cancelled: Cancel
    open --> on_hold: Place On Hold (Client Delay)
    on_hold --> open: Resume Work
    open --> completed: Complete (All Tasks Done)
    on_hold --> completed: Complete
    completed --> closed: Close (Financials Reconciled)
    completed --> open: Reopen (Defect Rectification)
    open --> cancelled: Cancel
    on_hold --> cancelled: Cancel
    closed --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

1. Projects Directory (/admin/projects)

  • Filterable list displaying Project Code, Title, Customer Name, Status (Draft, Open, On Hold, Completed, Closed, Cancelled), Budget Amount, Total Billed, and Target Completion Date.

2. Project Creation Form (/admin/projects/new)

  • Header: Project Title, Project Code (auto-generated e.g. PRJ-2026-0012), and Description.
  • Customer Assignment: Bind to a commercial client or mark as an Internal Company Project.
  • Dates & Currency: Estimated Start Date, Target Completion Date, and Contract Currency (KES, USD).
  • Budget Formulation: Target contract billing amount and estimated expense ceiling.

3. Project Detail Workspace (/admin/projects/[id])

  • Executive KPI Tiles:
  • Contract Budget: Total agreed revenue from customer.
  • Invoiced to Date: Amount billed via milestone invoices.
  • Materials Cost: Value of inventory items issued to the project.
  • Realized Gross Margin: Profit percentage earned on the project.
  • Action Toolbar: Contextual state buttons based on current status (Open Project, Put On Hold, Resume, Mark Completed, Close Project).
  • Task & Milestone Manager:
  • Interactive task checklist (e.g. Site Assessment, Mounting Rails Installation, Inverter Wiring, Testing & Commissioning).
  • Task state badges: Open, Completed, Cancelled.
  • Linked Documents Panel: Direct links to generated Sales Quotes, Sales Orders, Material Requisitions, and Customer Invoices.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Creating and Opening a Turnkey Project

  1. Navigate to /admin/projects and click New Project.
  2. Enter Project Title: "Solar PV Installation - 5kVA System".
  3. In the Customer lookup, select "Dr. Evans Mutiso".
  4. Enter Contract Budget: KES 650,000.00.
  5. Set Start Date: Tomorrow's date; Target Completion: 10 days later.
  6. Click Save Draft. Status becomes Draft.
  7. In the Tasks section, click Add Task:
  • Task 1: "Site Survey & Structural Roof Check".
  • Task 2: "Solar Panels Mounting & Conduit Piping".
  • Task 3: "Inverter & Lithium Battery Wiring".
  • Task 4: "KPLC Net-Metering Commissioning & Client Sign-Off".
  1. In the top action bar, click Open Project.
  2. The status transitions to Open. Team members can now issue stock and record time against the project.

Action 2: Completing Tasks and Milestone Invoicing

  1. When technicians complete the roof mounting, open /admin/projects/[id].
  2. Locate Task 2: "Solar Panels Mounting".
  3. Click the checkmark icon to Mark Completed.
  4. The task status updates to Completed.
  5. Click Generate Milestone Invoice in the action bar.
  6. The system opens the invoice builder pre-populated with the client's details, referencing Project #PRJ-2026-0012.
  7. Enter Milestone 2 amount: KES 325,000.00 (50% payment).
  8. Post the invoice. The project workspace immediately reflects: "Invoiced to Date: KES 325,000.00 (50%)".

Action 3: Closing a Fully Reconciled Project

  1. When all tasks are finished and the client signs the completion certificate:
  2. In the top action bar, click Mark Completed.
  3. Status moves to Completed.
  4. Review the final financial summary card:
  • Total Invoiced: KES 650,000.00
  • Actual Material Costs: KES 412,000.00
  • Direct Labor Expenses: KES 45,000.00
  • Net Gross Profit: KES 193,000.00 (29.7% Margin).
  1. Click the Close Project button.
  2. An InlineConfirm prompt appears: "Formally close project PRJ-2026-0012? No further expenses or lines may be posted."
  3. Click Confirm Closure. The status transitions to Closed.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

State Machine Restrictions

  • A project can only be Closed if its current status is Completed. An Open or On Hold project cannot jump directly to Closed.
  • If defects or post-installation warranty claims arise after completion, an authorized manager may click Reopen Project, moving the status from Completed back to Open.
  • A project in Closed status is immutable: no new tasks, material requisitions, or invoices can be attached.

---

Guide 09: Vendor Management, Procurement & Payables (/admin/vendors)

The Vendor Management & Procurement module orchestrates the complete Procure-to-Pay (P2P) lifecycle. It encompasses vendor prequalification, sealed competitive quotation rounds (RFQs), purchase orders, Goods Received Notes (RGN), automated 3-way invoice matching, landed cost capitalization, vendor payment vouchers, Accounts Payable ageing, anti-fraud bank account controls, and KRA Withholding Tax certificates.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Procurement Fraud & Inflated Supplier Invoices: In traditional businesses, suppliers submit invoices that charge higher prices than originally quoted, or bill for 100 units when only 80 arrived. Accounts departments often pay these blindly. QSell enforces strict Automated 3-Way Matching: a supplier invoice cannot be posted unless its line quantities and prices match the original Purchase Order (PO) and the physical Goods Received Note (RGN) within configured tolerance limits.
  • Vendor Bank Account Impersonation Fraud: The single most common corporate cybercrime occurs when a fraudster hacks a supplier's email and requests that pending invoice payments be sent to a "new bank account". QSell eliminates this through Mandatory Bank Change Quarantine: changing a vendor's bank details triggers a phone call-back verification protocol, secondary managerial approval, and a 72-hour payment cool-off period.
  • Hidden Import & Freight Costs: Importing goods involves sea freight, port clearance, customs import duty, and local transport. If these expenses are treated as general overhead rather than capitalized into the product's unit cost, the business underprices its goods and loses money. QSell's Landed Cost Apportionment wizard automatically divides freight and duty across product unit costs based on weight or value.
  • Statutory Withholding Tax (WHT) Penalties: Kenyan tax law requires companies to withhold 2% VAT or 3%/5% Income Tax from vendor payments and remit it to KRA. QSell calculates withholding tax automatically on every payment voucher and generates monthly KRA Withholding Certificates in one click.

Target Client Profiles

  • Importers & Large Distributors: Managing container shipments, customs clearing agents, and multi-supplier product lines.
  • Manufacturing & Assembly Plants: Procuring raw materials, packaging, and sub-components via competitive RFQs and blanket contracts.
  • Corporate Enterprises & Institutions: Requiring formal procurement compliance (requisitions, multi-quote comparisons, separation of duties).

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you take total control of your company's spending. You eliminate procurement fraud before it happens. Your buyers can run sealed competitive quote rounds through our Vendor Self-Service Portal; your warehouse receives goods with digital Goods Received Notes; and your finance team never pays a single shilling until our system proves that the invoice matches the purchase order and the warehouse delivery note. Furthermore, our anti-fraud bank change security protects you against CEO and supplier wire fraud."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% 3-Way Match Assurance: Eliminates over-billing and paying for missing goods.
  • Automated Landed Costing: True inventory valuation ensures selling prices maintain required profit margins.
  • Zero KRA Withholding Tax Fines: Automated calculation and certificate generation ensure full compliance with the Tax Procedures Act.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    CAT[1. Procurement Categories & Document Types Configured] --> VEND[2. Vendors Registered & Prequalified]
    VEND --> RULE[3. Ordering & Payment Rules Established]
    RULE --> POST[4. Vendor Posting Groups & AP Accounts Mapped]
    POST --> SEC[5. Anti-Fraud Bank Change Call-Back Policy Activated]
  1. Procurement Categories: Defined under /admin/vendors/categories (e.g. Raw Materials, Office Supplies, Logistics).
  2. Document Types: Compliance mandates set under /admin/vendors/document-types (e.g. KRA Tax Compliance Certificate, Business Permit).
  3. Vendor Accounts: Created or invited under /admin/vendors.
  4. Payment Rules & Tax Codes: Withholding VAT and Income Tax percentages set under /admin/vendors/payment-rules.
  5. Vendor Posting Groups: Linked to General Ledger Accounts Payable under Finance > Posting Setup.
  6. Required Permissions: vendors:read, purchase_orders:read/write, rgn:read/write, supplier_invoices:read/write, vendor_payments:read/write.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Procure-to-Pay (P2P) pipeline spans 25 operational sub-modules:

graph TD
    subgraph Sourcing["1. Sourcing & Qualification"]
        PRE["Vendor Prequalification & Review Queue"]
        RFQ["Requests for Quotation (Sealed Rounds)"]
        CONT["Blanket Contracts & Price Locks"]
        DOC["Expiring Compliance Documents"]
    end

    subgraph Purchasing["2. Ordering & Goods Receipt"]
        REQ["Purchase Requisitions"]
        PO["Purchase Orders (Draft -> Approved -> Sent)"]
        RGN["Received Goods Notes (RGN / GRNI Accrual)"]
        RTV["Goods Sent Back (Return to Vendor)"]
    end

    subgraph Payables["3. Invoicing & Settlement"]
        INV["Supplier Invoices (3-Way Matching)"]
        MEMO["Credit Memos & Vendor Refunds"]
        VOUCH["Payment Vouchers (Dual Approval)"]
        WHT["Withholding Tax Certificates"]
        BANK["Anti-Fraud Bank Account Controls"]
    end

    Sourcing --> Purchasing
    Purchasing --> Payables

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

1. Vendors Directory (/admin/vendors)

  • Master supplier cards: Company Name, KRA PIN, Primary Contact, Category, Prequalification Tier, Credit Terms (e.g. Net 30), and Balance Owed.

2. Requests for Quotation / RFQs (/admin/vendors/rfqs)

  • Competitive bidding engine:
  • Create an RFQ for specific items or services.
  • Invite prequalified vendors to submit sealed bids through the Vendor Portal.
  • Comparison Sheet: Side-by-side bid matrix comparing unit prices, delivery lead times, and payment terms.
  • Award the winning vendor and auto-generate the Purchase Order in one click.

3. Purchase Orders (/admin/vendors/orders)

  • Legally binding purchase commitments:
  • Header: Vendor, Delivery Warehouse, Target Delivery Date, Currency.
  • Lines: SKU, Quantity, Agreed Price, Tax Class.
  • Lifecycle: Draft $\rightarrow$ Pending Approval $\rightarrow$ Released $\rightarrow$ Sent to Vendor $\rightarrow$ Confirmed $\rightarrow$ Partially Received $\rightarrow$ Fully Received $\rightarrow$ Closed.

4. Received Goods / RGN (/admin/vendors/receipts)

  • Goods Receipt Note (RGN):
  • When the delivery truck arrives, warehouse staff inspect physical boxes.
  • Record line-by-line acceptance (e.g. Ordered: 100, Received Good: 95, Damaged: 5).
  • Automatically posts the accounting accrual: Dr Inventory / Cr Goods Received Not Invoiced (GRNI).

5. Supplier Invoices (/admin/vendors/invoices)

  • The 3-Way Matcher:
  • Vendor submits their invoice via the Vendor Portal (or staff type it in).
  • System automatically links the invoice lines to the corresponding RGN and PO lines.
  • Flags price variances, quantity discrepancies, or duplicate invoice numbers.

6. Landed Costs (/admin/vendors/landed-costs)

  • Import cost capitalization: Apportions shipping freight, marine insurance, and customs duty across received product lines by weight, volume, or value.

7. Payments to Vendors (/admin/vendors/payments)

  • Payment voucher management:
  • Select approved due invoices.
  • Automatically deducts Withholding Tax (WHT).
  • Routes voucher for Dual Managerial Approval before initiating bank EFT transfer or M-Pesa B2B payout.

8. What We Owe / Payables Ageing (/admin/vendors/payables)

  • Accounts Payable ageing report: Current, 1-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, 90+ days overdue, with printable vendor statements.

9. Vendor Scorecards (/admin/vendors/scorecards)

  • Automated supplier rating based on: Delivery on-time %, quality acceptance rate (% goods rejected at RGN), and price stability.

10. Anti-Fraud Bank Changes (/admin/vendors/bank-changes)

  • Controlled quarantine for vendor bank account edits:
  • Flags any request to update payment details.
  • Requires telephone call-back verification to the vendor's primary registered landline.
  • Requires 2nd senior manager sign-off.
  • Enforces a mandatory 72-hour payment cool-off quarantine before funds can be disbursed to the new account.

11. Petty Cash Floats (/admin/vendors/petty-cash)

  • Office expense float management: Imprest float balance, petty cash expense vouchers with scanned receipts, float replenishment workflows, and GL account allocation.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Receiving Goods and Generating a Goods Received Note (RGN)

  1. Navigate to /admin/vendors/receipts and click New Goods Receipt.
  2. Select the Purchase Order (e.g. PO-2026-0038 from "SolarTech Kenya Ltd").
  3. The lines auto-populate with the ordered items: "100 units of 500W Panels".
  4. Enter the vendor's physical Delivery Note Number (e.g. DN-88192).
  5. In the Received Qty column, type 100.
  6. If 2 panels are shattered upon inspection, enter Accepted: 98, Rejected: 2, and select Rejection Reason: "Physical Transit Damage".
  7. Click Post Goods Receipt (RGN).
  8. The system updates warehouse stock immediately by 98 units, posts the GRNI accrual in the general ledger, and generates formal PDF RGN documentation for the delivery driver.

Action 2: 3-Way Matching and Booking a Supplier Invoice

  1. Navigate to /admin/vendors/invoices and click New Supplier Invoice.
  2. Select Vendor: "SolarTech Kenya Ltd".
  3. Type the Vendor's Invoice Number: INV-99410.
  4. Link the invoice to RGN #RGN-2026-0024.
  5. The system performs the 3-Way Match:
  • PO Price: KES 12,000.00 per panel.
  • Invoice Price: KES 12,000.00 per panel. $\rightarrow$ MATCH
  • RGN Accepted Qty: 98 units.
  • Invoice Billed Qty: 98 units. $\rightarrow$ MATCH
  • Tax Rate: 16% VAT. $\rightarrow$ MATCH
  1. Green badges confirm: "3-Way Match Passed (0% variance)".
  2. Click Post Supplier Invoice.
  3. The document transitions to Posted, moves into Accounts Payable, clears the GRNI accrual, and books the liability to Vendor Payables.

Action 3: Processing an Anti-Fraud Vendor Bank Account Change

  1. Navigate to /admin/vendors/bank-changes.
  2. A pending request appears: "SolarTech Kenya Ltd submitted new bank details: Equity Bank, Acc #011223344".
  3. The system locks all pending payment vouchers for SolarTech Kenya Ltd.
  4. The Procurement Officer dials the vendor's registered landline telephone (taken from the original prequalification certificate, not from the email request).
  5. After confirming the legitimacy of the change with the vendor's Managing Director, the officer enters the Call-Back Verification Code and notes.
  6. The Finance Director opens the request and clicks Approve Bank Change.
  7. The system initiates the 72-Hour Cool-Off Period. A countdown timer displays on screen: "Payments to this account unlock in 71h 59m", preventing immediate wire transfers.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

The Automated 3-Way Matching Tolerance Rule

  • If the price billed on a supplier invoice exceeds the purchase order price:
  • If variance $\le \text{Configured Tolerance}$ (e.g. 0.5% or KES 50), the system permits booking with a price adjustment log.
  • If variance $> \text{Configured Tolerance}$, booking is blocked until the procurement manager issues an approved Purchase Order Amendment or the vendor submits a corrected invoice.

Duplicate Invoice Protection

  • The system enforces a strict composite database unique constraint: (vendor_id, LOWER(TRIM(vendor_invoice_number))).
  • If an accountant attempts to enter an invoice number that already exists for that vendor (even with extra spaces or different letter casing), the system blocks the entry with the message: "Invoice [Number] has already been booked for this vendor on [Date]."

---

chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 10: Finance, General Ledger & Accounts Receivable (/admin/finance)

The Core Finance & Accounts Receivable module provides a complete, double-entry financial accounting system with the discipline of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. It encompasses the Chart of Accounts, General Journals, immutable G/L Entries and Registers, Real-Time Trial Balances, Fiscal Periods, the Posting Setup Matrix, Customer Receipts Allocation, Customer Wallets (Store Credit), Safeguarded Refunds, Foreign Exchange Revaluation, and Debtor Ageing.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The Month-End "Disappearing Debtors" Hunt: In traditional systems, sales invoices, cashier receipts, and warehouse dispatches are recorded in separate tables that frequently disagree with the general ledger. Accountants spend weeks chasing discrepancies between the Accounts Receivable sub-ledger and the G/L balance. QSell guarantees Sub-Ledger and G/L Invariant Harmony: every invoice, receipt, return, and wallet credit is posted together with its balancing G/L double entries in the exact same atomic transaction.
  • Accidental Back-Dated Posting Chaos: A rogue or untrained user edits an invoice from three months ago, throwing off previously certified and tax-audited financial statements. In QSell, Posted Means Immutable. Past journal lines can never be edited or deleted. Errors must be corrected by formal reversals or credit memos with mandatory reason logging. Furthermore, closed fiscal periods are cryptographically locked.
  • Overpayment & Customer Credit Chaos: When a customer pays KES 10,000 for an KES 8,000 order, most systems treat the extra KES 2,000 as a negative debt or loose money. QSell features a native Customer Wallet Sub-Ledger: unallocated overpayments or return credits are securely parked in the customer's digital store wallet as a clean liability, ready to automatically offset future purchases.
  • Refund Embezzlement & Fraud: Internal staff frequently issue unauthorized cash refunds to personal phone numbers. QSell enforces a Separation of Duties Refund Framework: refunds require dual managerial approval, mandatory upload of supporting evidence, phone-number velocity limits, and daily payout caps.

Target Client Profiles

  • Corporate CFOs, Financial Controllers & Chief Accountants: Demanding IFRS-compliant double-entry accounting, audit-ready journal registers, and instant drill-down from financial statements to source transactions.
  • High-Volume Retail & Wholesale Distributors: Managing thousands of customer invoices, partial payments, credit notes, and multi-currency transactions.
  • B2B Trade Merchants: Managing credit customers with strict 30/60/90-day payment terms and debt collection schedules.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you get the financial rigor and posting discipline of tier-one enterprise ERPs like Microsoft Dynamics Business Central, built specifically for modern African businesses. There are no batch delays and no month-end reconciliation surprises. The second a cashier rings up a sale or an M-Pesa payment confirms, your General Ledger, Accounts Receivable sub-ledger, and Trial Balance update simultaneously. Your books are permanently audit-ready, your customer store wallets are automated, and your refund payouts are locked with anti-fraud limits."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Zero Reconciliation Hunting: General Ledger control accounts and Accounts Receivable balances match at all times.
  • 100% Audit Integrity: Append-only ledger registers record Who, What, When, Why, and From Where for every shilling.
  • Guaranteed Fraud Protection: Segregation of duties prevents the person creating a credit memo or refund from approving or disbursing the payout.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    COA[1. Chart of Accounts Defined] --> POST[2. General Posting Setup Matrix Configured]
    POST --> PER[3. Fiscal Calendar Periods Opened]
    PER --> WAL[4. Customer Credit & Wallet Policy Set]
    WAL --> LIMIT[5. Refund Anti-Fraud Limits Assigned]
    LIMIT --> TRANS[6. Financial Invoicing & Postings Active]
  1. Chart of Accounts: Defined under /admin/finance/accounts (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, COGS, Expenses).
  2. Posting Setup Matrix: Configured under /admin/finance/posting-setup (Mapping which G/L accounts receive sales revenue, inventory, tax, and receivables postings).
  3. Fiscal Calendar: Periods opened under /admin/finance/periods (At least one active open accounting period).
  4. Customer Credit & Wallet Policy: Defined under /admin/finance/receivables/wallet-policy.
  5. Refund Limits: Defined under /admin/finance/refunds/limits.
  6. Required Permissions: gl_accounts:read, journals:read/post, ledger_registers:read, trial_balance:read, receipts:read/create, refunds:read/act.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Finance architecture coordinates the General Ledger and Accounts Receivable sub-ledgers:

    end

        AR[Customer Sub-Ledger: customer_detailed_entries]

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Part A: General Ledger (/admin/finance)

1. Chart of Accounts (/admin/finance/accounts)

  • Master list of accounts organized by category: 1000 Assets, 2000 Liabilities, 3000 Equity, 4000 Revenue, 5000 Cost of Goods Sold, 6000 Operating Expenses.
  • Account configuration: Account Code, Account Name, Account Type (Posting, Heading, Total), Direct Posting Toggle, Blocked Status, and Balance Sheet / Income Statement mapping.

2. General Journals (/admin/finance/journals)

  • Manual journal preparation workspace:
  • Create balanced debit and credit entries with Document Number, Posting Date, G/L Account, Description, Amount, and Dimension Sets (Branch, Department).
  • Posting Preview: Runs the complete posting simulation in memory and renders every entry that would be created before writing to the database.

3. G/L Entries (/admin/finance/entries)

  • The immutable general ledger: Search and filter millions of ledger lines by Account, Date, Document No, or Register ID. Shows Debit, Credit, and Source Document link.

4. Postings / Registers (/admin/finance/registers)

  • The master audit log: Each row represents one atomic posting event, recording Register No, Starting/Ending Entry ID, Posting Date, User ID, Source Document, and Reason Code.
  • Reverse Transaction Action: Reverses an entire register with an equal-and-opposite posting in one click with mandatory reason capture.

5. Trial Balance (/admin/finance/trial-balance)

  • Real-time trial balance report: Filter by Date Range, Dimension (Branch/Cost Center), or Account Group. Shows Opening Balance, Period Net Movement (Debits/Credits), and Closing Balance. Total Debits strictly equal Total Credits.

6. Fiscal Periods (/admin/finance/periods)

  • Fiscal calendar management: Configure 12 monthly periods per fiscal year. Set period status (Open, Soft-Closed, Closed, Locked). Prevents back-dated postings into audited periods.

7. Posting Setup (/admin/finance/posting-setup)

  • The business-to-accounting translation matrix: Maps product business classifications, customer groups, and payment methods to specific G/L accounts (e.g. Retail Hardware Sales $\rightarrow$ Account 4100; Wholesale Cement Sales $\rightarrow$ Account 4200).

---

Part B: Accounts Receivable (/admin/finance/receipts, /admin/finance/receivables)

8. Receipts (/admin/finance/receipts, /new)

  • Customer payment recording:
  • Select Customer, Payment Method (Cash, Bank Transfer, Cheque, M-Pesa), Amount Paid, and Payment Reference.
  • Invoice Allocation Grid: Displays customer's open unpaid invoices. Allows auto-allocating payment to oldest invoices first, or manually selecting specific invoices to settle.

9. Customer Wallets (/admin/finance/receivables/wallets)

  • Customer store credit liability sub-ledger:
  • Displays customer wallet balances.
  • History of wallet funding (overpayments, returned goods, cash advances) and redemptions against orders.

10. Credit Adjustments (/admin/finance/receivables/credit-adjustments)

  • Manual adjustments to customer balances (bad debt write-offs, courtesy credits):
  • Requires mandatory 2nd-person managerial approval before affecting the general ledger.

11. Customer Refunds & Limits (/admin/finance/refunds, /limits)

  • Payout governance:
  • Multi-tier refund request workflow (Request $\rightarrow$ Verification & Evidence $\rightarrow$ Approval $\rightarrow$ Disbursement).
  • Anti-Fraud Limits: Sets maximum daily refund amount per customer phone number, per cashier, and per branch.

12. Receivables Ageing (/admin/finance/receivables/ageing)

  • Debtor analysis dashboard: Buckets outstanding customer debt into Current, 1-30 Days, 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days, and 90+ Days. Drill down to individual overdue invoices to trigger dunning notices or pause credit accounts.

13. Foreign Exchange & Revaluation (/admin/finance/exchange-rates)

  • Multi-currency rate table and month-end FX revaluation wizard: Automatically calculates and posts unrealized foreign exchange gains or losses on foreign currency receivables (USD, EUR, GBP) to the G/L.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Recording and Allocating a Customer Payment

  1. Navigate to /admin/finance/receipts and click New Receipt.
  2. In the Customer lookup, select "Nairobi Hardware Wholesalers".
  3. Enter Amount Received: KES 150,000.00.
  4. In the Payment Method dropdown, select "Bank Transfer - KCB".
  5. In the Reference box, enter the bank deposit slip number: DEP-99412.
  6. The screen displays the customer's unpaid invoices:
  • Invoice #INV-1002: Balance KES 80,000.00.
  • Invoice #INV-1008: Balance KES 50,000.00.
  • Invoice #INV-1014: Balance KES 40,000.00.
  1. Click Auto-Allocate (Oldest First).
  2. The system allocates KES 80,000 to INV-1002 (paid in full), KES 50,000 to INV-1008 (paid in full), and the remaining KES 20,000 to INV-1014 (partial payment, KES 20,000 remaining).
  3. Click Post Receipt.
  4. The receipt is posted. General ledger entries are generated instantly (Dr KCB Bank / Cr Accounts Receivable), and official payment receipts are generated.

Action 2: Posting a General Journal with Posting Preview

  1. Navigate to /admin/finance/journals and open the "General Operations" batch.
  2. Click Add Journal Line:
  • Account: 6100 - Office Electricity & Water.
  • Side: Debit, Amount: KES 18,500.00.
  • Description: "March Power Bill - Head Office".
  1. Click Add Balancing Line:
  • Account: 1120 - Petty Cash Float.
  • Side: Credit, Amount: KES 18,500.00.
  1. Click the Posting Preview button in the header.
  2. The preview modal renders showing the exact G/L entries that will be written, proving debits equal credits.
  3. Click Confirm & Post Journal.
  4. The register number is generated (REG-2026-0182), entries are written to gl_entries, and the batch clears.

Action 3: Reversing an Erroneous Financial Posting

  1. Navigate to /admin/finance/registers.
  2. Locate the register created in error (e.g. REG-2026-0182).
  3. Click View Register Details.
  4. In the top action bar, click Reverse Register.

Post customer transactions through customer invoices, receipts, or credit memos to preserve sub-ledger integrity."

Fiscal Period Locking Rules

  • If an accounting period is set to Closed or Locked (e.g. December 2025):
  • Any transaction dated within that period is strictly rejected.
  • Transactions must have their posting date moved into the earliest open fiscal period.

Guide 11: Banking, Cash & Payment Gateways (/admin/finance/bank-accounts, /admin/payments, /admin/currencies)

The Banking, Cash & Payment Gateways module governs the physical and digital cash flow of the business. It encompasses commercial bank accounts, physical cashier cash drawers, Safaricom M-Pesa merchant integrations (STK Push, Paybill, Till, and Bill Manager), automated bank statement CSV reconciliations, multi-currency exchange rates, and raw integration audit logs.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The "Missing M-Pesa Payment" Nightmare: In typical businesses, customers send money to a Paybill number, but network drops or customer typos mean the order remains "Unpaid" on the screen while funds are deducted from the customer's phone. Staff argue with customers and manually check Safaricom statement portals. QSell provides Real-Time Payment Activity Telemetry: every inbound webhook, STK prompt, and transaction payload is captured live. If an orphan payment arrives, the Reconciliation Workspace matches it to the pending order with a single click.
  • Cash Till Shortages & Till Theft: In busy retail stores, cashiers collect physical cash notes all day. Without strict controls, till shortages are discovered days later when it is impossible to identify which cashier was responsible. QSell mandates End-of-Day Cash Drawer Counts: cashiers count their physical notes (KES 1,000s, 500s, 200s, 100s, 50s, coins) against the system's expected book balance, and variances are automatically flagged and posted.
  • Manual Bank Statement Reconciliation: Financial controllers spend days each month printing bank statements and ticking off line items against customer deposits. QSell features an Automated Bank Statement CSV Reconciler: upload a standard bank statement, and the system automatically matches deposits to open invoices and customer ledger entries based on reference numbers, dates, and amounts.
  • Exposing API Keys in Plaintext: Many platforms store payment provider API keys and consumer secrets in unencrypted configuration files. QSell encrypts all API credentials at rest in the database with hardware-grade cryptographic sealing; keys are never exposed on screen or printed in server logs.

Target Client Profiles

  • High-Velocity Omnichannel Retailers: Processing hundreds of M-Pesa and card transactions hourly across in-store POS and web shop.
  • Multi-Branch Store Networks: Operating independent bank accounts and cash drawers per branch location.
  • Cross-Border Regional Traders: Invoicing and collecting in multiple currencies (KES, USD, EUR, UGX, TZS) with daily exchange rate revaluations.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you will never lose track of a single payment. We integrate natively with Safaricom M-Pesa (both STK Push and Bill Manager), major Kenyan banks, and card processors. When a customer pays, your books update immediately. If a network blip occurs, our payment activity dashboard shows you the raw gateway response in real time. And at the end of every day, your cashiers conduct digital till counts that verify physical cash against book sales down to the last five-shilling coin."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% Payment Ingress Visibility: Zero lost mobile-money transactions; orphan payments matched in seconds.
  • Instant Till Shortage Detection: Physical cash variances highlighted before cashiers leave the premises.
  • Zero API Credential Exposure: Sealed cryptographic storage ensures bank and M-Pesa secrets cannot be stolen.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    CURR[1. Currencies Configured: KES Base, USD, EUR] --> BANK[2. Bank Accounts & Cash Drawers Created]
    BANK --> PROV[3. Payment Providers Configured: M-Pesa, Banks, Cards]
    PROV --> METH[4. Payment Methods Bound to Operating Branches]
    METH --> RECON[5. Daily Bank Statements & Till Counts Active]
  1. Currencies Active: Base currency (KES) and foreign currencies established under /admin/currencies.
  2. Bank Accounts Created: Defined under /admin/finance/bank-accounts (Commercial banks and physical tills).
  3. Payment Providers Configured: Credentials entered under Settings > Payments.
  4. Public Base URL Set: Company or branch must have a valid public HTTPS URL configured so gateway webhooks can reach the server.
  5. Staff Permissions: bank_accounts:read/write, cash_counts:read/create, payment_activity:read, transactions:reconcile.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Banking and Payment ecosystem is structured into three operational layers:

graph TD
    subgraph Ingress["1. Ingress & Settlement Channels"]
        STK["M-Pesa STK Push (Online / POS)"]
        C2B["Paybill / Till C2B Inbound"]
        BILL["M-Pesa Bill Manager (E-Invoices)"]
        CARD["Credit / Debit Cards (Pesapal)"]
        CASH["Cashier Physical Till Drawers"]
    end

    subgraph Telemetry["2. Activity & Audit Telemetry"]
        ACT["Payment Activity Webhook Stream"]
        AUDIT["Integration Audit Log (Payload Inspector)"]
        TRANS["Raw Transaction Ledger"]
    end

    subgraph Reconciliation["3. Financial Reconciliation"]
        RECON["Payment Reconciliation Matcher"]
        STMT["Bank Statement CSV Import"]
        TILL["End-of-Day Cash Till Counts"]
        GL["General Ledger Bank Posting"]
    end

    Ingress --> Telemetry
    Telemetry --> Reconciliation
    Reconciliation --> GL

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

1. Bank Accounts (/admin/finance/bank-accounts)

  • Master directory of corporate liquid funds:
  • Commercial Bank Accounts (e.g. KCB, Equity Bank, Standard Chartered).
  • Mobile Money Settlement Accounts (Safaricom M-Pesa Paybill / Buy Goods Till).
  • Physical Cash Drawers (e.g. Till #1 - Westlands, Till #2 - Mombasa).
  • Displays real-time Book Balance, Last Reconciled Date, Currency, and Status.

2. Bank Statements & Reconciliation (/admin/finance/bank-statements)

  • Reconciles bank reality with general ledger books:
  • Upload official bank statement CSVs.
  • Interactive split screen: Statement Lines on the left; System Bank Ledger Entries on the right.
  • Auto-Match Button: Matches transactions by Reference ID, Date, and Shilling Amount.
  • Unmatched transactions can be posted directly as bank charges, interest income, or direct customer deposits.

3. Cash Counts (/admin/finance/cash-counts)

  • End-of-shift retail till verification:
  • Select Branch and Cash Drawer.
  • Enter physical denomination counts (Quantity of KES 1,000, 500, 200, 100, 50, 40, 20, 10, 5, 1).
  • Displays Expected Balance vs. Counted Balance, calculating exact Shortage or Overage.
  • Posts variance adjustment entries with mandatory supervisor approval.

4. Currencies & FX (/admin/currencies)

  • Multi-currency management: Base currency (KES) and foreign currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, UGX, TZS).
  • Maintain daily spot exchange rates and view monthly FX revaluation logs.

5. Transactions Ledger (/admin/transactions/ledger)

  • Low-level payment record: Shows every payment attempt, gateway transaction ID, channel, customer phone number, monetary value, and settlement status (Pending, Paid, Failed, Reconciled).

6. Payment Activity (/admin/payments/activity)

  • Real-time developer & operations log: Displays live stream of incoming gateway webhook notifications from Safaricom Daraja, banks, and card processors.
  • Essential for customer care desks investigating delayed or disputed payments.

7. M-Pesa Bill Manager Invoices (/admin/payments/bills)

  • Push electronic bills directly to customer Safaricom M-Pesa apps:
  • Select customer invoice.
  • Send M-Pesa Bill Manager notification.
  • The customer receives an official Safaricom notification on their phone displaying invoice details and a single "Pay Now" prompt.
  • Receipting is 100% automated upon PIN entry.

8. Reconciliation (/admin/reconciliation)

  • The orphan payment matching engine:
  • Lists payments received by M-Pesa or bank transfer that could not be automatically matched to an order (e.g. customer entered wrong account number).
  • Search pending customer orders and click Manually Match & Settle to instantly confirm the order.

9. Integration Audit Log (/admin/integration-audit)

  • Deep forensic payload viewer: Inspect the complete HTTP headers, request payloads, and response bodies for every outbound API call and inbound webhook.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference
