---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Reconciling an Orphan M-Pesa Payment to an Order

  1. A customer calls claiming they paid via M-Pesa Paybill, but their web order still shows "Pending Payment".
  2. Navigate to /admin/reconciliation.
  3. In the Unmatched Payments table, search by the customer's phone number or the M-Pesa transaction code (e.g. QA9912048X).
  4. The payment is located: "KES 4,500.00 received at 11:42 AM from 0712345678".
  5. In the Candidate Orders pane on the right, the system automatically suggests Order #ORD-10928 based on matching phone number and shilling amount.
  6. Click Link Payment to Order.
  7. An InlineConfirm prompt appears: "Match transaction QA9912048X (KES 4,500.00) to Order ORD-10928?"
  8. Click Confirm Match.
  9. The order status updates instantly to Paid, stock is reserved, a confirmation SMS is sent to the customer, and the payment is marked reconciled in the transaction ledger.

Action 2: Executing an End-of-Day Cash Till Count

  1. At store closing, the cashier navigates to /admin/finance/cash-counts and clicks New Cash Count.
  2. Select Cash Drawer: "Till #1 - Westlands".
  3. The system shows that the cashier's till is locked for new sales during counting.
  4. Count the physical banknotes and enter the counts:
  • KES 1,000 notes: 45 ($= \text{KES } 45,000$)
  • KES 500 notes: 12 ($= \text{KES } 6,000$)
  • KES 200 notes: 8 ($= \text{KES } 1,600$)
  • KES 100 notes: 15 ($= \text{KES } 1,500$)
  • Coins: KES 240.00
  1. Total Counted calculates: KES 54,340.00.
  2. System Book Balance shows: KES 54,350.00 (Variance: - KES 10.00 Shortage).
  3. In the explanation box, enter: "Small coin shortage due to change deficit".
  4. Select the Supervisor Witness and click Submit & Close Till.
  5. The count is saved, the till is closed, and an adjustment journal for KES 10.00 is posted to the Cash Shortage expense account.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

Payment Provider Webhook Signature Verification

  • Inbound webhooks from payment gateways (Safaricom Daraja, Pesapal) are cryptographically validated against sealed company secrets.
  • Any request lacking a valid HMAC signature or originating from an unauthorized IP address is rejected immediately with HTTP 401 and logged in the Integration Audit Log as a security incident.

Reconciling Multi-Currency Bank Accounts

  • A bank account denominated in USD can only be reconciled against statement CSVs in USD.
  • When customer payments in USD are allocated to KES invoices, the system automatically uses the active spot exchange rate and writes any currency conversion discrepancy to the Foreign Exchange Gain/Loss G/L Account.

---

Guide 12: Approvals & Internal Controls (/admin/approvals, /admin/settings/approvals)

The Approvals & Governance module delivers a zero-code, runtime corporate approval engine inspired by Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. It allows administrators to define, version, simulate, and enforce approval hierarchies across purchase orders, price discounts, sales credit limits, inventory adjustments, and customer refunds—with tiered signing limits, automatic substitute rerouting, and real-time bottleneck monitoring.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Rigid, Hard-Coded Approval Rules: In most software, if a board of directors changes the purchase order signing limit from KES 100,000 to KES 250,000, software developers must be paid to rewrite and redeploy code. QSell's approval rules are 100% Runtime Configuration: administrators change thresholds, add approvers, or toggle approval rules on or off in seconds with zero downtime.
  • Operational Gridlock When Managers Travel: In traditional organizations, business grinds to a halt when the Managing Director goes on leave or travels abroad without connectivity; urgent purchase orders and customer deliveries sit unapproved. QSell features native Substitute Approver Chains: if a designated manager is on leave, requests automatically route to their certified substitute, or escalate to the next qualified manager after a configurable due-time threshold.
  • In-Flight Workflow Corruption: In legacy systems, editing an approval rule while orders are currently pending either crashes the system or leaves documents in an orphaned "limbo" state. QSell uses Immutable Versioned Workflows: active in-flight documents complete under the exact workflow version they started with, while new requests seamlessly use the updated version.
  • Unexplained Approval Rejections: Managers often reject employee requests without explanation, creating workplace frustration and delayed customer service. QSell enforces Mandatory Reason Codes and Comments: an approver cannot click "Reject" without selecting a standardized reason code and providing an explanatory note.

Target Client Profiles

  • Corporate Enterprises & Institutions: Requiring strict financial governance and tiered signing authorities (e.g. Supervisor up to KES 50k, Manager up to KES 250k, Director Unlimited).
  • Multi-Branch Retail Chains: Requiring localized approval hierarchies (e.g. Mombasa store manager approves Mombasa write-offs, while Head Office approves capital expenditures).
  • Audit-Regulated Organizations: Subject to internal and external financial control audits (ISO 9001, IFRS, Sarbanes-Oxley).

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you enforce total financial discipline without slowing down your business. You can set up multi-step approval workflows for large purchase orders, high discounts, or stock write-offs without writing a single line of code. If your Commercial Director is out of office, the system automatically routes the request to their appointed deputy. And our visual Approval Monitor gives you complete visibility over what is waiting on whom, highlighting bottlenecks before they delay a customer."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% Zero-Code Workflow Maintenance: Modify signing limits and approvers in seconds without IT developer costs.
  • Zero Document Deadlock: Automated timeout escalations prevent documents from stalling during executive absence.
  • Complete Governance Audit Trail: Every approval, rejection, delegation, and escalation is timestamped and permanently logged.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    USERS[1. Staff Accounts & Hierarchy Created] --> PROF[2. Approver Profiles & Amount Limits Assigned]
    PROF --> GRP[3. Approver User Groups Configured]
    GRP --> WORK[4. Workflows Designed with Triggers & Steps]
    WORK --> SWITCH[5. Module & Scenario Switches Activated]
    SWITCH --> SIM[6. Workflow Simulation Verification]
  1. Staff Directory: Users must exist under /admin/users.
  2. Approver Profiles & Limits: Configured under /admin/settings/approvals/approvers (Assigning signing limits and substitutes).
  3. Approver Groups: Configured for multi-person approval committees (e.g. Tender Committee).
  4. Workflow Designer: Built under /admin/settings/approvals/workflows.
  5. Switches: Toggled active under /admin/settings/approvals/switches.
  6. Required Permissions: approvals:act to approve/reject; approvals:request to submit; approvals:manage to design workflows.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Approvals engine separates operational tasks from administrative configuration:

graph TD
    subgraph Operations["Front-Office Operations (/admin/approvals)"]
        INBOX["Waiting on Me (Actionable Inbox)"]
        MYREQ["My Requests (Submissions Tracker)"]
    end

    subgraph Administration["Governance Configuration (/admin/settings/approvals)"]
        WORKFLOWS["Workflow Designer & Versioning"]
        LIMITS["Approvers, Limits & Substitutes"]
        SWITCHES["Module & Scenario On/Off Switches"]
        MONITOR["Real-Time Bottleneck Monitor"]
    end

    Administration --> Operations

The Four Approver Resolution Types

When a document enters a workflow step, the engine resolves who must act based on one of four rules:

  1. Specific Approver / Group: Sent directly to a named individual or an ordered user committee (e.g. "Finance Director" or "Tender Committee").
  2. Requester's Line Manager: Sent to the direct supervisor of the person who initiated the document.
  3. Approver Chain by Limit: Evaluates the requester's supervisor; if the document amount exceeds their signing limit, it automatically climbs to their supervisor, and so on until a qualified approver is reached.
  4. First Qualified Approver: Skips intermediate managers and jumps directly to the first person up the chain whose signing limit covers the document amount.

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Part A: Front-Office Operations (/admin/approvals)

1. Waiting on Me (/admin/approvals/inbox)

  • The actionable executive queue: Displays all documents currently requiring the logged-in user's approval.
  • Summary columns: Document Type (Purchase Order, Sales Order, Credit Memo, Stock Write-Off, Customer Refund), Document No, Requester Name, Total Amount, Due In / Overdue indicator.
  • Action Buttons:
  • Approve: Instantly releases the document to the next step or final approved state.
  • Reject: Opens mandatory rejection modal requiring a reason code and explanatory note.
  • Delegate: Forwards the request to another qualified user or designated substitute.

2. My Requests (/admin/approvals/requests)

  • Personal submissions tracking: Shows documents submitted by the user that are currently in-flight.
  • Shows current step, assigned approver, submission date, and time elapsed.
  • Action: Cancel Request (withdraws the document back to Draft state before an approver acts).

---

Part B: Governance Configuration (/admin/settings/approvals)

3. Workflows (/admin/settings/approvals/workflows)

  • Visual workflow designer:
  • Trigger Catalogue: Select event (e.g. Purchase Order Released, Order Exceeds Credit Limit, Stock Count Variance > Threshold).
  • Condition Tree Builder: Build logical rules using AND / OR blocks (e.g. Order Amount > KES 100,000 AND Branch = Nairobi).
  • Step Sequence Builder: Add ordered approval steps, assign resolution rules, set due hours, and configure overdue behaviors (Remind, Escalate to Supervisor, Auto-Approve, Auto-Reject).
  • Dry-Run Simulator: Select a real past document and simulate the workflow in sandbox mode to preview who would be assigned.

4. Approvers & Limits (/admin/settings/approvals/approvers)

  • Matrix of staff signing authorities:
  • Assign maximum approval limits per document kind (e.g. John Kamau: PO Limit KES 200,000; Refund Limit KES 20,000).
  • Unlimited Checkbox: For executive directors.
  • Substitute Approver Picker: Assign an alternate staff member and activate substitute mode when traveling.

5. Switches (/admin/settings/approvals/switches)

  • Three-tier on/off control switches:
  1. Module Switches: Turn approvals on/off globally for an entire module (e.g. disable all Purchase Order approvals).
  2. Scenario Switches: Toggle specific triggers (e.g. enable Order Credit Limit Approvals, but disable Margin Floor Approvals).
  3. Branch Overrides: Apply switches to specific branches.

6. Monitor (/admin/settings/approvals/monitor)

  • Executive bottleneck control room:
  • Lists all approval requests currently in-flight across the entire company.
  • Highlights requests that are overdue against target SLAs.
  • Reassign Action: Super Admins can reassign stuck requests to an alternate manager to prevent operational delays.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

Workflow Step Fields (/admin/settings/approvals/workflows/[id])

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Step SequenceExecution order.IntegerSystemRe-orderable (1, 2, 3...).
Approver RuleHow approver is chosen.DropdownRequiredSpecific User, User Group, Line Manager, Chain by Limit, First Qualified.
Target User / GroupSelected actor or committee.Lookup AutocompleteRequired if SpecificIdentifies user or group.
Requirement RuleQuorum for group steps.DropdownRequired if GroupAny One Member, All Members Must Approve, N of Group.
Due After (Hours)SLA target window.Integer (Hours)RequiredNumber of hours before marked overdue (e.g. 24).
Overdue ActionWhat happens on SLA breach.DropdownRequiredRemind Only, Escalate to Next in Chain, Auto-Approve, Auto-Reject.
Self-ApprovalCan requester approve own request?Toggle (On/Off)RequiredDefault Off. Enforces strict separation of duties.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Reviewing and Approving a Purchase Order in the Inbox

  1. The Finance Manager logs in and navigates to /admin/approvals/inbox.
  2. A badge shows: "Waiting on Me (1)".
  3. Click the request: "Purchase Order #PO-2026-0042 from Acme Supplies (KES 380,000.00)".
  4. A slide-over drawer opens displaying the full purchase order document, vendor details, and the approval chain history.
  5. Inspect the line items and budget availability.
  6. Click the green Approve button in the header.
  7. A confirmation banner displays: "Purchase Order #PO-2026-0042 approved successfully."
  8. The document transitions to Approved, releases for procurement, and vanishes from the manager's pending inbox.

Action 2: Rejecting a Discount Request with a Mandatory Reason

  1. In the inbox, select a Sales Order discount request: "Order #ORD-1092 - 18% Discretionary Discount".
  2. The manager determines that 18% wipes out product margin.
  3. Click the red Reject button.
  4. The Rejection Modal appears (the action cannot proceed without it):
  • Select Reason Code: Unacceptable Margin Loss.
  • In the Mandatory Comment box, type: "Maximum allowable discount on this inverter model is 8%. Please revise quote with customer."
  1. Click Confirm Rejection.
  2. The request status updates to Rejected, the sales order reverts to Draft state, and an instant alert is sent to the sales representative with the manager's explanation.

Action 3: Reassigning a Stuck Document via the Approval Monitor

  1. A sales order for a priority customer is stuck because the designated Branch Manager is hospitalized.
  2. The Operations Director navigates to /admin/settings/approvals/monitor.
  3. Locate the stuck document, flagged in red: "Overdue by 42 hours (Assigned to: Peter Mwangi)".
  4. Click Reassign Request.
  5. Select New Approver: "Susan Kiprop (Regional General Manager)".
  6. Enter Reassignment Reason: "Emergency reassignment due to medical leave of primary approver".
  7. Click Confirm Reassignment.
  8. The request instantly transfers to Susan Kiprop's inbox, and the audit log records the emergency reassignment.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

The Self-Approval Block

  • By default, allow_self_approval = false.
  • If a Managing Director creates a Purchase Order, the system detects that Requester ID == Approver ID and automatically escalates the document to the Board Chairman or appointed second signatory.

In-Flight Workflow Immutability

  • When a workflow definition is edited and saved, the system creates a new version (e.g. Version 3).
  • Any document that was submitted under Version 2 will continue executing through the Version 2 step sequence until completion. New submissions automatically use Version 3.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

1Assign approval limit of KES 100,000 to Supervisor and Unlimited to Director.Limits accurately reflect on Approver Profiles screen.[ ]
2Build a Workflow for Purchase Orders exceeding KES 100,000.Workflow compiles cleanly with active trigger and steps.[ ]
3Submit a test PO for KES 150,000 as a Buyer.PO halts in Pending Approval and appears in Director's Inbox.[ ]

Guide 13: Settings, Branches, Numbering & KRA eTIMS (/admin/settings)

The Settings & Configuration module forms the bedrock of the entire enterprise deployment. It governs organizational Dimensions, physical operating Branches, Payment Provider integrations, gapless Number Series engines, Document Number Bindings, Order Stage Target Timers (SLAs), and complete Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA TIMS & eTIMS) fiscal compliance.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The KRA eTIMS Compliance Trap: Under Kenyan tax law, every B2B and B2C commercial invoice must be validated, digitally signed, and transmitted to the KRA eTIMS system in real time, complete with cryptographic control codes and verification QR codes. Businesses using legacy POS software must buy expensive external hardware "Type C" fiscal boxes (KES 40,000 to KES 80,000 per till) that regularly jam, drop serial connections, and halt store sales. QSell features native Direct Cloud eTIMS Digital Signing: no external boxes required; invoices sign in milliseconds via direct API integration.
  • Audit Disasters from Gapped Invoice Numbering: Tax auditors from the KRA routinely penalize businesses if invoice numbers contain missing gaps (e.g. INV-0012 followed by INV-0014 without an explanatory audit trail for 0013). QSell enforces Strict Gapless Number Series Engines: document numbers are reserved transactionally; if a transaction aborts, the gap is tracked or the sequence is preserved cleanly.
  • Multi-Branch Tax Inconsistencies: A company with branches in Nairobi, Mombasa, and Kisumu may have different physical fiscal devices or branch-specific KRA middleware. QSell supports Independent Branch Tax Modes: branches can either inherit the company-wide eTIMS configuration or operate under independent fiscal credentials.
  • Unnoticed Operational Sluggishness: Orders sit for hours between "Order Placed" and "Picking Started" without anyone noticing. QSell's Order Target Timers alert management when any stage exceeds its SLA threshold.

Target Client Profiles

  • Kenyan Retail & Wholesale Enterprises: Subject to mandatory KRA eTIMS invoice transmission and VAT compliance.
  • Multi-Branch Retail Chains: Requiring standardized document numbering (e.g. INV-NBI-0001 vs INV-MBA-0001) and localized branch reporting.
  • SLA-Sensitive Delivery & E-Commerce Merchants: Guaranteeing customers fast fulfillment and delivery windows.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, regulatory tax compliance and enterprise setup are solved out of the box. You do not need to buy expensive, unreliable fiscal gadget boxes for each of your cashiers. Our native KRA eTIMS integration signs and transmits your invoices in the cloud in real time, generating official QR codes on every printed receipt. Furthermore, our gapless number series protect you from tax audit penalties, and our multi-branch architecture lets you scale to 50 stores with complete central visibility."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% KRA eTIMS Compliance: Zero risk of non-compliance fines (saving up to KES 1,000,000 per violation).
  • Elimination of Fiscal Box Hardware Costs: Saves KES 50,000+ per counter till by utilizing software-based cloud signing.
  • Zero Gapless Audit Errors: Guaranteed sequential numbering satisfies statutory book requirements.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    DIM[1. Dimensions Configured: Cost Centers & Regions] --> BRAN[2. Physical Operating Branches Created]
    BRAN --> NUM[3. Number Series & Bindings Established]
    NUM --> SLA[4. Order Targets & SLA Timers Defined]
    SLA --> TAX[5. KRA Tax Classifications & eTIMS Mode Setup]
  1. Dimensions: Established under /admin/settings/dimensions (Optional financial tags).
  2. Branches: Created under /admin/settings/branches.
  3. Number Series: Formats defined under /admin/settings/number-series and bound under /admin/settings/number-series/bindings.
  4. Order Targets: SLA thresholds set under /admin/settings/order-targets.
  5. KRA eTIMS Mode: Configured under /admin/settings/tax-compliance/kra-tims-etims.
  6. Required Permissions: settings:read/manage, branches:read/manage, numbering:manage, taxes:manage.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Settings module is organized into six administrative domains:

graph TD
    subgraph Structure["1. Organizational Infrastructure"]
        DIM["Dimensions (Cost Centers, Territories)"]
        BRAN["Operating Branches & Banking Links"]
    end

    subgraph Numbering["2. Sequential Integrity"]
        NUM["Number Series (Prefixes, Resets, Padding)"]
        BIND["Document Bindings (Order, Invoice, PO)"]
    end

    subgraph ServiceLevel["3. Operational SLAs"]
        TARG["Order Stage Targets & Escalations"]
    end

    subgraph Compliance["4. KRA Tax & eTIMS Engine"]
        CLASS["Tax Classification (16%, 0%, Exempt)"]
        ITEMS["eTIMS Item Master Synchronization"]
        MODE["Company vs Independent Branch Mode"]
        LOG["Forensic Signing Log & QR Audit"]
    end

    Structure --> Numbering
    Numbering --> ServiceLevel
    ServiceLevel --> Compliance

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

1. Dimensions (/admin/settings/dimensions)

  • Multi-dimensional reporting axes: Create custom tags (e.g. Cost Center, Department, Project, Sales Territory).
  • Allows slicing Trial Balance, Sales Reports, and Expense Ledgers by dimension values without cluttering the Chart of Accounts.

2. Branches (/admin/settings/branches)

  • Physical business units:
  • Branch Code (e.g. BR-NBI-01), Branch Name (e.g. "Nairobi Central Depot").
  • Physical Street Address, City, County, GPS Coordinates.
  • Linked Default Cash Drawer and linked Bank Account.
  • Public Base URL configuration for localized payment gateway webhooks.

3. Payments (/admin/settings/payments)

  • Payment provider configuration:
  • Connect Safaricom M-Pesa Daraja APIs (Shortcode, Consumer Key, Consumer Secret, Passkey, B2C initiator credentials).
  • Connect Card Processors (Pesapal, Bank PGWs).
  • All secrets encrypted with AES-256 GCM sealed storage.

4. Number Series (/admin/settings/number-series)

  • Document sequential engine:
  • Define formats (e.g. Prefix INV-, Starting No 00001, Ending No 99999, Increment 1).
  • Configure Yearly Restarts (e.g. resetting sequence to 0001 on January 1st).
  • Enforce Gap-Less Rules for fiscal documents.

5. Document Numbering Bindings (/admin/settings/number-series/bindings)

  • Connects document types to specific number series per branch:
  • Branch Nairobi: Invoices bind to series INV-NBI-, Quotes bind to QT-NBI-.
  • Branch Mombasa: Invoices bind to series INV-MBA-, Quotes bind to QT-MBA-.

6. Order Targets & SLA Timers (/admin/settings/order-targets)

  • SLA management:
  • Define target duration per order stage (e.g. Picking: Max 45 mins, Packing: Max 30 mins, Delivery: Max 180 mins).
  • Configure notification triggers and escalation email alerts when orders languish in a stage.

7. Tax Compliance & KRA eTIMS (/admin/settings/tax-compliance)

The comprehensive regulatory suite divided into five sub-screens:

  1. Tax Classification (.../classification): Maps company tax categories to official KRA eTIMS tax codes:
  • Code A: Standard Rate (16% VAT).
  • Code B: Zero-Rated (0% VAT - exports, medicines).
  • Code C: Exempt (financial services, unmanufactured agricultural produce).
  • Code D: Special / Petroleum (8% Fuel VAT).
  1. eTIMS Items Master (.../items):
  • Synchronizes product catalog items with KRA's central item registry.
  • Shows registration status, KRA Item Code, packaging unit code, and stock sync status.
  • Action: Register Item with KRA, Update Item, Transmit Restock Notification.
  1. Signing Log (.../signing-log):
  • Forensic audit trail of every invoice signing attempt.
  • Displays Document No, Timestamp, Result (Signed, Skipped, Failed), KRA Invoice Code, Cryptographic Middleware Signature, and QR URL.
  • For skipped or failed documents, displays exact reason trace (e.g. "Skipped: Proforma quote is not a tax document" or "Failed: KRA VSCU endpoint timeout, retrying via outbox").
  1. Company Mode (.../company): Sets the global default mode: Disabled, TIMS (Hardware Control Unit), or eTIMS (Cloud Digital Signing).
  2. Branch Modes (.../branches): Overrides company mode for specific branches operating independently.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

Number Series Form Fields (/admin/settings/number-series/new)

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Series CodeIdentifier for this sequence.Text (Max 20 chars, uppercase)Requirede.g. SERIES-INV-2026.
DescriptionHuman-readable explanation.Text (Max 120 chars)Requirede.g. "2026 Sales Invoices Series".
PrefixCharacters leading the number.Text (Max 10 chars, uppercase)Requirede.g. INV- or PO-.
Starting NumberFirst sequential integer.IntegerRequiredTypically 1 or 1001.
Ending NumberCeiling for this series.IntegerRequiredMust be $>$ Starting Number. Generates warning at 95% capacity.
Padding LengthTotal digits with leading zeros.Integer (1-10)Requirede.g. 5 yields 00001, 6 yields 000001.
Allow GapsCan sequence skip cancelled numbers?Toggle (On/Off)RequiredMust be Off for KRA tax invoices and credit notes.

KRA Tax Classification Fields (/admin/settings/tax-compliance/.../classification)

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Tax LabelDisplay name in app.Text (Max 60 chars)Requirede.g. "General VAT (16%)".
Tax Rate %Percentage applied to line.PercentageRequirede.g. 16.0 or 0.0.
KRA TIMS CodeLegacy hardware tax code.Single Character (A-E)RequiredA=16%, B=0%, C=Exempt, D=Other, E=8%.
KRA eTIMS CodeCloud digital signing code.Text (Max 10 chars)RequiredStandard KRA HS item tax code.
Applies to DeliveryDoes delivery charge take this tax?Toggle (On/Off)RequiredDelivery fee is a service taxed at 16% VAT by default.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Creating a Branch-Specific Invoice Number Series

  1. Navigate to /admin/settings/number-series and click New Series.
  2. Enter Series Code: INV-MOMBASA-2026.
  3. Enter Prefix: INV-MSA-.
  4. Set Starting No: 1, Ending No: 99999, Padding Length: 5.
  5. Set Allow Gaps: Off (enforcing strict audit compliance).
  6. Click Save Number Series.
  7. Navigate to /admin/settings/number-series/bindings.
  8. Locate Document Kind: Tax Invoice, and find Branch: "Mombasa Retail Store".
  9. In the dropdown, change the binding from Global Series to INV-MOMBASA-2026.
  10. Click Save Bindings. All future invoices generated in Mombasa will print numbers formatted as INV-MSA-00001.

Action 2: Inspecting and Verifying the KRA Invoice Signing Log

  1. Navigate to /admin/settings/tax-compliance/kra-tims-etims/signing-log.
  2. The log renders in chronological order.
  3. Locate Invoice #INV-2026-00412.
  4. Inspect the columns:
  • Result: Signed (Green badge).
  • KRA Middleware Signature: eTIMS-KRA-01928374-AF892B.
  • Control Code: 0192-8374-AF89.
  1. Click View Signing Trace:
  • Gate 1 (Document): PASSED (Tax Invoice).
  • Gate 2 (Scope): PASSED (Company eTIMS Active).
  • Gate 3 (Customer): PASSED (Customer PIN Validated).
  • Gate 4 (Readiness): PASSED (Keys valid, response received in 240ms).
  1. Click the QR Code Preview link to test that scanning the QR code opens the official KRA tax invoice verification portal page.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

The 7-Gate KRA Invoice Signing Policy

Every invoice generated by the system passes through the 7-Gate Evaluation Policy in strict order:

  1. Document Gate: Proforma quotes and draft orders are never signed.
  2. Scope Gate: Evaluates whether the branch operates under independent mode or company mode.
  3. Mode Gate: eTIMS or TIMS must be configured for that scope.
  4. Mode Switch Gate: Signing must be enabled for that mode.
  5. Module Switch Gate: Invoicing module switch must be active.
  6. Customer Gate: Checks if customer explicitly opted out (diplomatic missions).
  7. Readiness Gate: Digital certificates must be valid and unexpired.

If any gate halts, the document records a Skipped or Failed event with an explicit reason string. Crucially, a temporary KRA network outage never halts customer sales: the invoice is issued locally, and the signing task is queued in the transactional outbox for automated background retry.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

StepVerification TaskExpected ResultPass/Fail
1Create Mombasa and Nairobi branches with unique codes.Branches appear in branch selection dropdowns across the system.[ ]
2Create sequential gapless Number Series for Invoices and POs.Numbers increment sequentially without skips.[ ]
3Configure KRA eTIMS Tax Classifications (16% VAT, 0%, Exempt).Product catalog reflects mapped tax codes accurately.[ ]
4Post a test cash sale invoice and inspect KRA Signing Log.Document signs successfully; QR code and KRA signature code generated.[ ]
5Verify Order Stage SLA target timers.Lapsed orders in Packing stage trigger late warning alerts on dashboard.[ ]

Guide 14: External & Field Portals (/(store), /rider, /vendor)

While administrative staff manage operations via /admin, QSell delivers three purpose-built external interfaces: the Customer Web Storefront (/(store)), the Rider Mobile App (/rider), and the Vendor Self-Service Portal (/vendor). These portals extend the system's core capabilities directly to shoppers, field delivery crews, and supply chain partners.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Customer Phone Ordering Friction: Customers have to call or WhatsApp sales reps to inquire about stock availability, ask for prices, and track their delivery status. The Customer Storefront empowers shoppers to browse live stock, calculate exact delivery charges via map pin drops, checkout via M-Pesa, and track their order's timestamped progress in real time.
  • Rider Paper Run Sheets & Misplaced Delivery Notes: Delivery riders traditionally carry loose paper receipts and invoices on their motorbikes, which get stained by rain, torn, or lost. The Rider Mobile App delivers an interactive, mobile-optimized daily run sheet directly to the driver's smartphone, complete with one-tap Google Maps directions, customer phone dialing, and digital proof-of-delivery PIN verification.
  • Supplier Invoice Phone Tag & Lost Invoices: Suppliers regularly email invoices that get trapped in spam filters or sit forgotten on buyers' desks, resulting in delayed orders and supplier relationship friction. The Vendor Portal enables prequalified suppliers to log in, view open RFQs, submit competitive price bids, acknowledge purchase orders, and generate electronic supplier invoices matched directly to Goods Received Notes.

Target Client Profiles

  • Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) & B2B Web Merchants: Selling to both retail end-consumers and trade account holders on one unified website.
  • Last-Mile Logistics Fleets: In-house motorcycle dispatchers, delivery vans, and third-party contract drivers.
  • Multi-Vendor Procurement Networks: Sourcing materials from tens or hundreds of trade vendors and service contractors.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, your business operations connect seamlessly to the outside world. Your customers shop on a fast, modern web store customized with your brand and colors. Your delivery riders carry our dedicated mobile app that guides them stop by stop and verifies deliveries using customer SMS PINs. And your suppliers manage their bids, orders, and invoices in their own private portal—giving you an enterprise ecosystem without paying for external third-party software licenses."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Zero Third-Party Portal Subscription Costs: Built-in customer storefront, rider dispatch, and vendor portals eliminate separate SaaS subscriptions.
  • 100% Secure Tenant Isolation: External users are cryptographically restricted to their own session records; vendors can never see competing bids or internal staff notes.
  • Paperless Field Operations: Digital run sheets, doorstep PINs, and electronic delivery notes eliminate paper loss.

---

2. Prerequisites & Portal Access Setup

graph TD
    COMP[1. Company Profile, Logo & Brand Colors Configured] --> STORE[2. Storefront Catalog & Payment Providers Live]
    STORE --> RIDER[3. Riders Added; Riders with Their Own Account Given a Phone Number and PIN]
    RIDER --> VEND[4. Vendors Invited to Register on Vendor Portal]
  1. Branding & Gateways: Storefront appearance, payment providers, and delivery zones must be configured in /admin.
  2. Sellable Products: Catalog items must have Show on Web Shop = True and active selling prices.
  3. Rider Logins: Riders are added under /admin/delivery/riders. A rider with an account of their own needs a Kenyan mobile number, and the office gives them a PIN there (see Guide 06, Action 4). A member of staff who rides signs in with their own email and password.
  4. Vendor Portal Access: Vendors must receive an invitation link or register at /vendor/register.

---

3. Architecture of the Three External Surfaces

graph LR
    subgraph Storefront["Customer Storefront (/(store))"]
        CAT[Product Catalog & Search]
        CART[Shopping Cart & Wishlist]
        CHK[Pin-on-Map Checkout & M-Pesa]
        TRK[Real-Time Order Tracking]
    end

    subgraph RiderApp["Rider Mobile App (/rider)"]
        AUTH[Rider Phone Number and PIN Sign-In]
        RUNS[Active Run Sheets & Multi-Drop Stops]
        POD[Customer Delivery Code & Proof of Delivery]
        COD[Door Cash & M-Pesa Collection]
    end

    subgraph VendorPortal["Vendor Portal (/vendor)"]
        PRE[Prequalification Application]
        BID[RFQ Bidding & Quote Submission]
        PO[Purchase Order Acknowledgment]
        INV[Direct Invoice Generation against RGN]
    end

    Storefront --> APP["QSell Central Platform"]
    RiderApp --> APP
    VendorPortal --> APP

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Part A: Customer Web Storefront (/(store))

1. Home & Catalog (/)

  • Brand header, promotional announcement banners, search bar with live autocomplete, and mega-menu categories.
  • Responsive product cards displaying Title, Brand, Star Rating, Price (KES), Unit of Measure, Stock Availability Badge, and Add to Cart button.

2. Shopping Cart & Wishlist (/cart, /wishlist)

  • Line item quantity adjusters, subtotal calculation, coupon code entry box, and shipping fee estimator.

3. Checkout (/checkout)

  • The frictionless, single-page checkout flow:
  1. Customer Information: Name, email, mobile phone number.
  2. Delivery Method & Location:
  • Choose Delivery or In-Store Pickup / Click & Collect.
  • Drop a GPS pin on the map or select County $\rightarrow$ Town $\rightarrow$ Estate.
  • System calculates exact delivery fee in real time.
  1. Payment Selection: Safaricom M-Pesa STK Push, Credit/Debit Card, or Cash on Delivery.
  2. Order Submission: Dispatches M-Pesa prompt directly to customer's phone and transitions to order tracking upon PIN entry.

4. Order Tracking (/track/[id])

  • Customer self-service portal: Displays real-time progress bar through the order stage timeline (Order Confirmed $\rightarrow$ Preparing in Warehouse $\rightarrow$ Out with Rider $\rightarrow$ Delivered).
  • Displays the delivery code (6 digits) to give to the rider upon arrival, the promised delivery window until it is delivered, and a link to the courier's own page when a courier handles the parcel.

---

Part B: Rider Mobile Web App (/rider)

1. Rider Sign-In (/rider/sign-in, /rider/pin)

  • Clean, high-contrast mobile interface designed for one-handed operation on low-end smartphones.
  • Sign in (/rider/sign-in) with the rider's Kenyan mobile number and a 6-digit PIN (no password to type with gloves on). Opening /rider while signed out leads here. A link underneath offers email and password sign-in for staff who ride.
  • Choose your own PIN (/rider/pin): the PIN the office gives is temporary, and the rider must replace it with their own before anything else in the app opens. The same screen (Change my PIN) is used later.
  • Five wrong tries in a row shut the rider out for a while (15 minutes, growing to 4 hours); the office can let them try again at once. A PIN opens the rider app only, and only for riders with an account of their own.
  • Sign out is at the top of every screen.

2. Active Run Sheet (/rider and a run's own page)

  • Displays the assigned multi-drop run for the day:
  • Header: Run Number, Total Stops (e.g. "Stop 2 of 5"), Total Cash Float, Total Run Weight.
  • Ordered stop cards: Customer Name, Phone, Delivery Address, Estimated Arrival Time, Payment Method (Paid Online vs Collect KES 3,500 at Door).
  • Action: Open Google Maps / Waze Directions, Call Customer.

3. Delivery Confirmation & Door Payment (on a stop of the run)

  • Execution of the handover:
  • Input field for the customer's 6-digit delivery code (when the company's rule at the door asks for it).
  • Door Payment collection confirmation (Cash received or M-Pesa Paybill confirmation code).
  • Digital signature capture or photo upload of delivered parcel.
  • Action: Confirm Delivery or Report Failed Attempt (with mandatory reason selection).

4. My Pay (/rider/pay)

  • The rider's own pay: Owed to me now, Earned this month, the latest 30 pay entries (each Paid or Not paid yet; pay the office took back shows as Taken back by the office) and the latest 10 payouts. A rider sees only their own pay. See Guide 06.

---

Part C: Vendor Self-Service Portal (/vendor)

1. Registration & Prequalification (/vendor/register, /vendor/prequalification)

  • Supplier onboarding:
  • Complete legal business profile, KRA PIN, physical address, and bank wire details.
  • Select procurement categories applied for (e.g. Electrical Supplies, Solar Inverters).
  • Upload mandatory compliance documentation (Certificate of Incorporation, KRA Tax Compliance Certificate, CR12).

2. RFQ Bidding Workspace (/vendor/(portal)/rfqs)

  • View active Requests for Quotation invited to bid on.
  • Enter unit prices per line item, lead time in days, payment terms, and validity dates.
  • Submit sealed bid before the published round deadline.

3. Purchase Orders & Acknowledgment (/vendor/(portal)/orders)

  • View official purchase orders issued by the company.
  • Download official PDF Purchase Orders.
  • Action: Acknowledge PO (confirms commitment to deliver by promised date).

4. Supplier Invoicing (/vendor/(portal)/invoices)

  • Direct electronic invoice submission:
  • Select the matching Goods Received Note (RGN) issued by the warehouse.
  • Type vendor invoice number and attach invoice PDF.
  • Submit directly into the back-office 3-Way Match queue.

5. Withholding Tax Certificates (/vendor/(portal)/certificates)

  • Self-service tax portal: Suppliers can search by month and download official KRA Withholding VAT and Withholding Tax certificates without calling the accounts department.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

Storefront Checkout Fields (/(store)/checkout)

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Full NameRecipient identity.Text (Max 120 chars)RequiredRecipient of the package.
Phone NumberContact & payment phone.Phone (Max 25 chars)RequiredM-Pesa phone number e.g. 0712345678.
Delivery AddressPhysical location description.Text (Max 160 chars)Required if DeliveryLandmark, estate, apartment/house number.
Map Pin LocationExact GPS coordinates.Map Pin DropperOptionalUsed for precise distance rate calculation.
Payment MethodIngress payment choice.Radio SelectorRequiredM-Pesa STK Push, Credit Card, Cash on Delivery.
Customer Order NotesSpecial delivery instructions.Text (Max 300 chars)Optionale.g. "Call upon arrival at the security gate".

Rider Proof of Delivery Fields (on a stop of a run)

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Delivery code6-digit customer security code.Numeric (6 digits)Required when the company's rule at the door asks for the codeMatches the code sent to the customer when the delivery left.
Cash CollectedMonetary sum taken at door.Currency (KES)Required if CODVerified against order balance. Added to rider custody.
M-Pesa Trans IDDoorstep M-Pesa receipt code.Text (10 chars, uppercase)Required if Door M-PesaValid Safaricom receipt e.g. QA81273918.
Recipient NamePerson accepting parcel.Text (Max 80 chars)RequiredCustomer or authorized agent at premises.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Shopper Checkout with M-Pesa STK Push

  1. A customer browses the storefront, adds a "Solar Charge Controller" to the cart, and clicks Checkout.
  2. Fills in Name and Mobile Phone: 0712 345 678.
  3. Selects Delivery: Picks County: Nairobi, Estate: Westlands. The system quotes delivery fee: KES 250.00.
  4. Selects Payment Method: M-Pesa STK Push.
  5. Clicks the Place Order & Pay button.
  6. The screen displays a loading spinner: "Prompt sent to your phone. Please enter your M-Pesa PIN."
  7. Within 3 seconds, the customer's phone vibrates with the Safaricom STK prompt: "Do you want to pay KES 4,750.00 to [Company Trading Name]?"
  8. The customer enters their PIN.
  9. The checkout screen automatically detects payment confirmation, displays a green success checkmark, and redirects to /track/[orderId] displaying the 6-digit delivery code.

Action 2: Rider Executing a Delivery Stop on Mobile

  1. The delivery rider opens /rider on their mobile phone and signs in with their phone number and 6-digit PIN (on the first time after the office gives a PIN, they choose their own).
  2. The active run sheet displays: "Stop 1: Jane Wanjiku - Westlands".
  3. Clicks Navigate to open Google Maps turn-by-turn directions.
  4. Upon arrival, clicks I Have Arrived.
  5. Hands the parcel to Jane Wanjiku and asks for her 6-digit delivery code.
  6. Types the code (for example 048213) into the app.
  7. Clicks Complete Delivery.
  8. The app vibrates with a success chime, marks Stop 1 completed, and automatically queues Stop 2.

Action 3: Vendor Submitting an Electronic Invoice via the Vendor Portal

  1. The supplier logs into /vendor.
  2. Navigates to Orders & Receipts.
  3. Locates Purchase Order #PO-2026-0038 and clicks Create Supplier Invoice.
  4. The system pre-fills the screen with the quantities and prices from Goods Received Note #RGN-2026-0024.
  5. Types their company's internal invoice number: INV-SOLAR-8819.
  6. Uploads their signed invoice PDF.
  7. Clicks Submit Invoice to Accounts.
  8. The invoice immediately appears in the back-office queue at /admin/vendors/invoices ready for 3-way matching and payment.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Security Boundaries

Strict Vendor Data Isolation

  • Vendor Portal users are cryptographically restricted to their own corporate entity:
  • Every database query automatically applies WHERE vendor_id = session.vendor_id.
  • Vendors cannot see other vendors, competing bid prices, internal buyer notes, or uninvited RFQs.
  • Passing an arbitrary vendorId in the URL or payload is rejected with an instant security exception.

Rider Cash Custody Block

  • If a delivery rider has unremitted cash custody exceeding their maximum allowed cash ceiling (configured per rider under /admin/delivery/riders), the system blocks the dispatcher from assigning the rider to new delivery runs until previous cash is reconciled at the cashier desk.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

StepVerification TaskExpected ResultPass/Fail
1Complete a storefront checkout using M-Pesa STK Push.Order created; payment confirmed; customer receives SMS with tracking PIN.[ ]
2Open /track/[id] on a mobile browser.Order stage timeline renders with live milestone indicator and verification PIN.[ ]
3Log into /rider on a mobile device using a test rider PIN.Assigned delivery run sheet renders cleanly with stop sequence.[ ]
4Complete a test delivery stop using verification PIN.Delivery confirmed; status updates to Delivered across admin and customer tracking.[ ]
5Invite a test supplier to the Vendor Portal.Supplier registers, accesses open PO, and submits an invoice successfully.[ ]
